scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men and a head-covered woman in blue, olive and earth-colored robes look attentively up toward the left beneath an olive tree. Sunlit stone houses, flowers, a blue lake and purple hills surround them in a textured watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The four followers and Galilean village are an imaginative setting for the listeners addressed in this verse. Their attentive, wondering faces suggest receiving Jesus' declaration that He had found such great faith in no one in Israel. Jesus remains entirely outside the image; the painting does not attempt to portray His amazement directly. The people's precise appearances and gestures are artistic choices, not details supplied by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three elderly bearded men recline among smiling guests around a low table with bread, figs, grapes, and clay cups. Travelers approach on winding paths from both sides of a flowering garden terrace beneath olive branches and a grapevine arbor, with soft hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative banquet pictures the promised gathering from east and west. The three central elders represent Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; the reclining guests reflect the verse's meal imagery. Their appearances, the garden, and the food are artistic inventions, not a revealed description of heaven. Jesus is outside the frame.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed adults grieve outside closed wooden doors edged with amber light in a stone arch. A seated man covers his eyes, a bowed figure folds their arms, and a tearful foreground man clenches his fists and teeth. Indigo darkness surrounds the warm ochre and terracotta watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The closed, light-edged doorway and grieving adults in darkness form an imaginative setting for the verse's judgment, not a reconstruction of an event or the architecture of the afterlife. Tears, the covered face and clenched teeth relate to weeping and gnashing; the sealed threshold conveys being cast out. No figure represents Jesus or God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling young man in a long cream tunic sits upright on a low bed in a warm stone room. One hand rests on the bedding and the other opens on his knee. His bare feet rest on a woven mat; a clay jug and cup stand beside him, and an open doorway reveals a sunlit courtyard and olive leaves.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative room scene focuses on the verse's reported result: the servant restored that very hour following Jesus' word to the centurion. His joyful posture and simple furnishings are artistic choices, not details stated in the verse. Jesus and the centurion remain outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An older woman with closed eyes and flushed cheeks reclines on a low bed beneath an ochre blanket. She wears a cream headcloth and long-sleeved garment, with both hands resting on the blanket. A water jug and bowl stand beside her in a warm stone-and-plaster room with an open wooden door.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The view into the room imagines the moment Jesus enters Peter's house and sees her fever. Jesus remains outside the frame. The bed, household vessels and warm daylight are imaginative setting details, not details specified by the verse. Her reclining illness belongs to this verse; the picture does not advance to her healing.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling, head-covered woman in a terracotta dress and olive wrap sets a clay cup on a low wooden table while holding a plate of flatbread. A rumpled bed, water jug and woven basket stand in a sunlit stone-and-plaster room.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The picture imagines the woman's service after Jesus healed her: she stands beside the bed with bread and a cup. Jesus remains outside the frame. The household setting, food and expression are artistic details, not specified in the verse; the earlier touch and departing fever are not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: At dusk, a seated man and kneeling woman clasp hands beside a lamplit stone doorway. An older woman smiles nearby while villagers support a man and carry another on a woven stretcher. Olive branches frame the pink evening sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined evening courtyard places Jesus beyond the doorway, outside the picture. The gathering, supported sick and grateful faces connect the verse's bringing, healing and deliverance. The figures and setting are illustrative; unseen spirits and His spoken word are not given invented visible forms.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a stone courtyard at dusk, a gray-bearded man sits on a woven mat beneath a blanket. A woman in rose kneels beside him with a hand on his arm; a woman in olive stands behind. They look upward left with grateful expressions. A closed scroll, clay vessels, olive branches and a lit oil lamp surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The courtyard and unnamed people are imaginative, not patients identified in this verse. Their relieved expressions and restored posture evoke Jesus taking infirmities and bearing diseases. Jesus remains outside the frame; the companion offers support, not healing. The closed scroll recalls Isaiah's prophetic words without inventing visible text.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor crowd in earth-colored robes gathers beneath a tree beside a wooden boat. A man holds a coiled mooring rope while another stands at the gunwale. Clear blue water stretches toward low hills and a village on the far shore.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The crowd, waiting boat and visible far shore imaginatively connect Jesus' command with departure for the other side. Jesus remains outside the image. The boat, rope work, tree and distant village supply a plausible setting; this verse itself does not describe those details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in an ochre robe, rust-colored mantle and cream headcloth holds a tied scroll and raises an open hand beside a winding stone-lined path through olive trees. A pale village and blue hills lie beyond in warm watercolor light.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The scribe addresses Jesus entirely outside the frame. His closed scroll suggests his occupation, while the continuing path evokes his promise to follow wherever the Teacher goes. His appearance and the landscape are imaginative details; the image does not claim he fulfilled his promise.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream robe and rust mantle stands on a rocky path, one hand on his chest and the other open. An olive tree, a small hillside burial entrance, wildflowers and distant stone houses sit beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The disciple's open hand imagines his request to Jesus, who remains outside the frame. The small rock-cut burial entrance recalls his wish to bury his father. This setting is imaginative; it does not establish when his father died or depict a burial taking place.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in an olive mantle stands on a sunlit rocky path, looking to the right with one palm open. Behind him, three robed mourners attend a linen-covered bier outside a rock-cut tomb beneath an olive tree. Golden hills, distant houses and a blue sky fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined listener pauses on a path while mourners attend a covered bier near a tomb. Jesus is outside the frame. The juxtaposition recalls His command to follow Him and let the dead bury their own dead; it does not claim this funeral was witnessed in the verse or that the man's response is recorded. The first 'dead' is understood figuratively, not as corpses performing a burial.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three men in earth-colored robes brace inside a wooden fishing boat as foaming waves spill over its sides. One grips the gunwale, one holds an oar, and one crouches beside ropes and a net. Rain crosses the dark sky above distant hills, with muted warm light at the horizon.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative view focuses on the great storm and the boat being swamped. Jesus, whom the verse says was sleeping, remains outside the frame; none of the visible men represents Him. The disciples' poses, rigging, rain and colors are artistic reconstruction, not additional details stated in this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of four robed men at a sunny lakeshore. One climbs over a wooden fishing boat's side while a man aboard clasps his hand; two others approach along the pebbled bank. A bench, coiled rope and oar fill the boat, with blue water and golden hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The disciples boarding together picture the verse's statement that they followed Jesus into the boat. Jesus is kept outside the image, imagined already aboard behind the viewer. The helping gesture, four visible disciples, calm lakeshore, garments and warm daylight are illustrative choices, not details specified by the verse. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three anxious, bearded men in earth-colored tunics lean forward inside a wooden boat amid foaming blue-green waves. The nearest reaches toward the foreground, another extends an open hand, and the third grips the side. A linen sail, ropes and storm clouds frame the textured watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The storm-tossed fishing boat is an imaginative setting for the disciples' urgent plea. Their reaching hands and anxious faces point toward Jesus outside the lower frame, suggesting their approach to wake Him. The image depicts their request for rescue, before the storm is calmed. The men's appearances, boat details and arrangement are imagined.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in cream, olive, and rust robes sit in a wet wooden boat, looking upward with tense, wondering faces. Slack linen sailcloth and coiled rope fill the foreground. Calm blue water reflects warm light beneath clearing gray clouds and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative view from inside the boat focuses on the great calm after Jesus' rebuke. Wet timbers, slack sailcloth, and lingering clouds recall the storm; the disciples' tense, wondering faces echo His question about fear and little faith. Jesus remains outside the frame. The arrangement of the men and the warm light are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in earth-colored tunics sit in a wet wooden fishing boat, looking in wonder toward something outside the frame. One grips the gunwale, one rests his hands on an oar, and one raises an open palm. A slack sail hangs above them; calm blue-green water and distant hills glow beneath clearing golden clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The boat, slack sail and clearing sky imaginatively situate the men's astonishment after the storm. Their attention turns toward Jesus beyond the frame; the calm water illustrates the winds and sea obeying Him. The three visible men and their gestures are illustrative choices, not a claim about their exact number or appearance.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of two fierce, bearded men in worn earth-colored robes emerging from rock-cut tombs beside a sunlit lakeside path. The nearer man stands wide-legged with an arm outstretched; limestone, grasses and trees frame the blue lake.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two men and tombs follow the verse directly; their fierce gestures across the path picture why travelers could not pass. The lakeside hillside, clothing, light and facial details are imaginative staging, not supplied historical particulars. Jesus remains beyond the frame; no deliverance from later verses is shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two anxious, bearded men in long, worn earth-toned robes stand beside pale rocks. One extends an open hand and cries toward the right; the other raises a hand near his chest. A sunlit path leads toward blue water and distant hills beneath a softly clouded sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two men and rocky lakeside setting imaginatively visualize the plural speakers crying out in fear to the Son of God. Their alarm and questioning gestures relate to the question about torment before the appointed time. Jesus is outside the frame. The number of men, landscape and poses are artistic choices; the image depicts their fearful appeal, not an act of torment.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor landscape shows many brown, pink, dark and spotted pigs grazing on a golden hillside beyond a broad rocky foreground, with an olive tree at left, small wildflowers and hazy blue hills under a clouded sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The feeding herd follows the verse directly, while the broad open ground conveys its distance. The hillside, light, vegetation and arrangement of individual animals are imaginative setting details. The illustration stays with the herd feeding and does not depict later events.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of two bearded men in long earth-tone robes crouched among pale rocks, raising open hands toward the right. Brown, gray and pale pigs graze on a grassy slope beside a blue lake, with leafy branches overhead and low hills in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The distressed men's gestures indirectly represent the demons' plea through afflicted people; the men are not depictions of the demons themselves. The grazing herd is the requested destination, and Jesus remains outside the image. The setting, clothing and gestures are imaginative reconstruction. The image does not show the demons departing or the pigs' later destruction. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor herd of brown, rose and charcoal pigs rushes down a dusty, rocky bank into splashing blue-green water. A leafy tree overhangs the slope; dry grasses, reeds and distant hills surround the broad lake. No people or text appear.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined lakeside viewpoint follows the herd's headlong descent in Matthew 8:32. Dust and white water convey the sudden rush; the verse's fatal outcome is approached indirectly, without depicting drowned bodies. Jesus' command and the spirits' departure remain outside the visible scene. The precise terrain, vegetation and colors are artistic choices rather than details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of two alarmed herdsmen at a stone city gateway. One bends forward, catching his breath; the other points toward the countryside while speaking to two men and a woman. Sunlit stone homes, a winding road, distant hills, and small flowers surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene focuses on the herdsmen fleeing to the city and reporting everything, including the matter of the demon-possessed men. The gateway, clothing, listeners, and gestures supply a plausible setting; the verse does not specify those details. The events they describe remain outside the image, and Jesus is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A worried crowd in earth-colored robes gathers outside a stone town. A gray-bearded man extends both open hands, while a man beside him gestures toward a sunlit road curving away through golden grass and olive trees. More townspeople approach from the gateway, with blue hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The gathered townspeople and their imploring gestures imagine the city asking Jesus to leave its region. Jesus remains outside the frame, where their attention is directed; the open road suggests the departure they request. The town, landscape, clothing, expressions and individual gestures are illustrative choices. The verse does not state their motives or describe an actual departure.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed men sit in a sunlit stone room. The man in olive lowers his gaze with one hand on his chest; the man in red looks upward to the side; the man in cream and brown bows his head with clasped hands. A clay jar stands beside them on a woven mat.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined listeners' troubled faces and chestward gesture suggest a response to Jesus' knowledge of evil thoughts. Jesus remains outside the frame. The room, number of listeners, poses and sunlight are artistic choices, not details stated by Matthew 9:4; the picture does not assert that they repented.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a man reclining on a woven wooden bed beneath an ochre blanket. Two men and a woman gather closely around him, all looking hopefully toward the upper right. A sunlit doorway, clay jars, basket, and hanging textile furnish the simple stone room.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The reclining man and companions looking toward an unseen speaker evoke the faith Jesus sees and the courage His forgiveness gives. The room, clothing, and three companions are imaginative details; Matthew 9:2 specifies neither their number nor this setting. Jesus remains outside the frame, and the man has not yet risen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of three bearded men in long robes and head coverings, seated with rolled scrolls in a stone-and-plaster room. One looks downward, another gazes to the side, and the third touches his beard. Clay jars rest in a wall niche above a woven floor mat.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The three scribes and their closed mouths imaginatively convey the inward accusation reported in the verse. Their solemn expressions suggest judgment without turning it into a spoken confrontation. Jesus remains outside the frame. The room, scrolls, exact number of men and individual poses are illustrative choices, not details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a blue tunic reclining on a woven mat beneath a cream blanket. Two robed men sit nearby, one touching his beard and the other extending an open palm. All look toward the left. Warm light enters through a stone doorway beside clay vessels and hanging baskets.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative domestic setting holds the moment of Jesus' question: the man remains on his mat while listeners ponder forgiveness and the command to rise and walk. The open doorway and path suggest walking without showing the later healing. Jesus stays outside the frame, and the picture does not attempt to make forgiveness visible. The setting and expressions are artistic details, not additional facts stated in the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man in a cream tunic and blue mantle walks toward the open doorway of a sunlit stone house. An olive tree shades the village lane, with pink flowers by the wall and a clay jar beside the entrance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The man's upright step toward a doorway pictures his rising and going to his own house. The village, clothing and house are imaginative setting details; the verse does not describe their appearance. Jesus is outside the frame.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A barefoot, bearded man in a cream tunic and rust mantle bends to lift a blue-edged woven mat inside a warm stone room. He looks upward with a joyful expression. Clay jars sit nearby, and an open wooden door reveals sunlit stone houses and a path.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined response to Jesus' command centers the man gathering his mat; Jesus remains outside the picture. The open doorway suggests going home. The verse presents the command as evidence of the Son of Man's authority on earth to forgive sins. The room and expression are artistic details; forgiveness is not portrayed as a visible object.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor crowd in earth-colored robes gathers beneath a leafy tree beside a stone doorway. An older man holds his chest; a tearful woman raises open palms. Others clasp their hands, look upward in wonder, or bow their heads in warm sunlight.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined courtyard and villagers give visual form to the crowd's response. Widened eyes, a hand over the heart, open palms and a bowed head suggest fear, wonder and praise. Their upward gaze expresses glorifying God; it does not place the witnessed event in the sky. The setting, faces and gestures are imaginative details, not specified by the verse. Jesus is outside the frame, and God is not visibly portrayed.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream tunic and rust-red mantle steps away from a shaded wooden tax booth toward a sunlit stone-lined road. A stool, bowl of coins and rolled parchment remain behind him; olive branches frame distant village houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Matthew stepping away from the tax booth imagines his response to Jesus' call to follow Him. Jesus remains outside the frame. The clothing, coins, booth design and village setting are illustrative details, not descriptions supplied by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Nine men in loose robes recline on cushions around a low wooden table, where two pass a bowl. Bread, olives, bowls, clay cups and a jug fill the table. Warm light enters an open doorway in a textured watercolor house interior.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household meal pictures the verse's tax collectors and sinners reclining together with Jesus and His disciples. Jesus remains outside the frame; the visible companions are not assigned individual identities or moral labels. The house, food, clothing and bowl-passing gesture supply an imaginative historical setting rather than details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of four robed men conversing outside a plaster house. A gray-bearded man extends an open hand toward a younger listener. Through the doorway, three men sit on cushions around a low table with bread, bowls and a clay jug.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The foreground exchange imagines Pharisees addressing disciples beside the meal they observed. The diners evoke the tax collectors and sinners named in the question without assigning moral status by appearance. Jesus remains outside the picture. The doorway, clothing and meal details are illustrative rather than details specified by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly physician checks the wrist of a weary man resting under an ochre blanket in a stone courtyard. A bowl, folded linen and pottery jar sit nearby; two men walk along a sunlit lane beyond the doorway.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined village physician checking a sick man's wrist visualizes Jesus' comparison of the healthy and the sick. The healthy walkers provide the contrast. This illustrates His teaching, without claiming that this particular consultation occurred. Jesus is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard beneath fig leaves, a seated man offers a clay cup and gestures toward a cushioned seat. A standing visitor holds one hand to his chest and the other to a wooden doorway post. Bread, cups and a pitcher rest on a low table.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The offered cup and open seat imaginatively express mercy and welcome, relating to Jesus' call to sinners. This courtyard encounter is an illustration of His teaching, not an event described in the verse. Neither neighbor represents Jesus, and clothing does not identify anyone as sinful. Sacrifice is not pictured; the verse's contrast remains in the explanation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of four robed men in a sunlit stone courtyard. Two stand looking right, one extending an open palm and the other resting his hand at his chin. At left, two sit beside bread and clay bowls; one holds a piece of bread. Leafy branches frame the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The standing men imaginatively represent John's disciples asking Jesus, who remains outside the image, why they and the Pharisees fast while His disciples do not. The seated men's bread makes that contrast visible. The courtyard, meal arrangement and individual appearances are illustrative choices; the verse does not specify them or supply Jesus' answer.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed men sit quietly around a low table with empty clay bowls and cups in a sunlit stone courtyard. An unoccupied woven cushion rests in front, and a leafy floral garland hangs above an open doorway.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined wedding courtyard illustrates the latter part of Jesus' comparison, rather than a recorded wedding event. The three quiet companions, empty bowls and unoccupied cushion evoke fasting after the bridegroom is taken away. The floral garland recalls the earlier celebration; Jesus is not portrayed.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A pale cloth patch curls away from a worn russet garment draped over a wooden bench, exposing a large frayed hole. A sewing basket, thread, clay jar and sunlit stone courtyard with an olive tree surround it.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined household still life illustrates Jesus' cloth comparison rather than a recorded event. The pale patch lifting away from the worn garment and the enlarged frayed opening picture the damage described; the setting and sewing objects are artistic choices.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A torn dark wineskin spills red wine across a sunlit stone ledge beside a full, tied tan wineskin in a woven basket. A clay jug, purple grapes and vine leaves frame the courtyard, with hills and pale buildings beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard still life illustrates the teaching through its objects: the split old wineskin loses its wine, while the intact fresh skin keeps its contents safe. The jug and grapes identify the wine setting. The arrangement is an illustration of the comparison, not a separate event narrated in the verse. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A gray-bearded man in a cream robe and brown, burgundy-edged mantle kneels on sunlit courtyard stones, lifting open hands toward the upper right. A man and woman stand behind him by a shaded doorway; leaves hang above and a clay jar rests on a low ledge.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The father's kneeling posture and open hands imagine the ruler's plea to Jesus, who remains beyond the right edge. The courtyard, clothing, and two witnesses are illustrative choices. His sorrow reflects his report that his daughter has died; his uplifted appeal expresses confidence that Jesus can restore her life. The restoration is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four men in cream tunics and earth-colored cloaks walk away along a sunlit stone village lane. A clay jar stands by a shaded wooden doorway; vines, olive branches and small flowers frame the path, with distant rooftops and hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The four walking men picture the disciples accompanying Jesus, who is kept out of view ahead with the man He follows. The doorway and curved village lane provide an imaginative setting for movement and companionship; the verse does not specify these architectural details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman in a terracotta robe, brown mantle, and cream head covering crouches on a warm stone lane. Her outstretched fingertips touch the knotted fringe of a cream garment entering from the right. Sunlit limestone walls and a leafy branch surround the quiet watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The stone lane, clothing, and woman's expression are imaginative details framing the verse's stated action: she approaches from behind and touches Jesus' garment fringe. Only the cloth is shown, keeping Jesus outside the picture. Her weary, intent expression suggests long suffering and hope; no visible bleeding or outcome beyond this verse is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A kneeling woman in a terracotta dress, blue mantle and ivory head covering reaches toward an ivory garment with tassels. Warm sunlight lights the stone lane, ocher walls and an olive branch; the garment wearer is outside the frame.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The reaching hand and nearby garment imagine the woman's inward expectation: if she only touches His garment, she will be healed. The small gap preserves anticipation rather than depicting a completed healing. The lane, colors and pose are artistic choices. Jesus remains outside the frame; only the garment is shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman in a cream head covering, teal robe and rust shawl looks upward with a tearful smile, one hand on her chest and the other on her covered lap. Sunlight warms a stone lane, doorway, clay jar and leafy branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Her relieved expression imagines the courage and restoration described in Jesus' words. Her gaze points toward Jesus outside the picture; He is not depicted. The kneeling posture, clothes and village lane are imaginative staging, not details specified by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two seated men play wooden pipes on a woven mat as mourners weep and raise their hands behind them. A timber doorway frames the warm plastered room, with clay vessels at the left and a small latticed window at the right.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined doorway view focuses on the flute players and crowd Jesus sees. The grieving faces and lamenting gestures interpret the commotion as mourning. The house, clothing and arrangement are artistic reconstruction; Jesus remains outside the frame.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A girl lies with closed eyes beneath a cream blanket on a low bed. Beside a sunlit doorway, two robed men laugh and look back toward the room; an older man and a woman look grave. Earthen jars, baskets, woven mats and warm plaster walls surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household places the still girl beside onlookers near the exit, two laughing toward Jesus outside the frame. Their mockery illustrates the response to His words that the girl is not dead but sleeping. The room, clothing and gestures are artistic reconstruction; the later raising is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a dark-haired girl in cream and rose robes rising from a low bed while holding an adult hand entering from the right. Several people stand outside an open doorway; clay jars and warm stone walls surround her.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The clasped hands and the girl's rising posture picture Jesus taking her hand and her arising. Only His hand and sleeve are shown. The people outside recall the crowd being put out. The bed, room, clothing and expressions are imaginative details, not additional facts stated in this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling traveler gestures as a veiled woman and an older man listen beside stone houses. A winding path passes other villagers and olive trees toward hilltop settlements beneath a pale blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The conversations and connected village paths imaginatively visualize the report spreading throughout the region. The verse names no particular messengers, houses, or route; those details illustrate the reach of the news. Jesus is outside the scene.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men with closed eyes walk along a sunlit stone village lane with wooden staffs. The man in a terracotta cloak extends an open hand; his companion in olive rests a hand on his upper arm. Both have open mouths. Olive branches and flowers frame the warm watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Their calling mouths, careful steps and outstretched hand imagine the two blind men following Jesus and pleading for mercy. Jesus remains outside the picture toward the right. The village lane, clothing, staffs and steadying hand are imaginative details, not specified by the verse. No healing is shown; their address, Son of David, belongs to the verse rather than a visible symbol.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men with closed eyes stand in a sunlit plastered house. The man in blue holds a hand to his chest and opens his other palm; the man in brown holds a wooden staff. A doorway, clay vessels, wooden bench and woven mat surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The men are imagined answering Jesus with trusting attention inside the house, before any healing is shown. Jesus remains outside the frame. Their gestures express the spoken affirmation, "Yes, Lord." The number two, clothing, furnishings, light and exact poses are illustrative choices; this verse refers to the blind men in the plural and does not specify these details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men with closed eyes sit side by side in olive and rust-colored robes as hands in cream sleeves gently touch their eyelids. Warm sunlight falls across textured plaster, a stone wall, a woven mat and a clay jug.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative domestic scene pictures two men receiving the touch at their closed eyes. Only the hands of Jesus enter the frame; the room, clothing and posture are reconstructed details, not details supplied by this verse. Their quiet expressions suggest trust, while the verse's spoken declaration is conveyed by the explanation rather than lettering.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in cream tunics and red and olive mantles sit with open eyes turned toward the upper right. One rests a hand on his chest; the other folds his hands in his lap. Golden light enters a wooden doorway beside textured plaster walls and a clay jar.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The men's open eyes evoke restored sight, while their hushed attention toward an unseen speaker relates to Jesus' stern command that no one should know. Jesus remains outside the image. The room, clothing and gestures are imaginative staging; the verse does not specify them or say here how the men later respond.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of two bearded men speaking with open-handed gestures to villagers on a sunlit stone lane. A seated man listens at left, while a woman and an older man stand at right. Olive trees, branching paths and hillside houses extend into the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two speakers and listening neighbors imaginatively picture those who went out and spread news about Jesus. Branching paths and distant settlements suggest the whole region. The verse does not specify these villagers, gestures or setting; Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed men support a weary, closed-mouthed man in a blue-gray tunic beside a sunlit stone doorway. All three look toward the right. Two smaller figures walk away along the lane behind them; vines and a clay jar frame the warm watercolor courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The companions bringing the man toward Jesus reflect the verse; Jesus remains outside the frame. The courtyard, clothing, supportive gestures and departing figures are imaginative staging. His closed mouth suggests his inability to speak; his demonic affliction is not given a visible form. This depicts his arrival, without showing a cure.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man in an olive tunic and brown wrap speaks with one hand on his chest and the other extended, surrounded by astonished villagers in a sunlit stone courtyard beneath leafy branches. Warm watercolor washes and fine contours texture the clothing and walls.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The speaking man and astonished listeners imagine the aftermath of the demon being cast out. The courtyard, clothing and individual gestures are artistic reconstruction rather than details stated in the verse. Jesus remains outside the frame; the demon is not visualized because the scene follows its expulsion.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in cream, ochre and blue-gray robes stand beside a wooden doorway and clay jar. One speaks with an outstretched hand while his companions listen seriously. Olive branches frame a sunlit stone village, painted in warm, textured watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative village composition focuses on the Pharisees speaking the accusation reported in the verse. The setting, clothing and gestures are illustrative choices, not details supplied by the verse. Jesus remains outside the frame, and no demons are shown; the picture does not present their claim about His power as true.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an elderly man in an ochre mantle standing beside a woman who holds his arm. Seated adults and a child look toward the right beyond the frame. Stone walls, wooden beams and woven mats surround them; a sunlit lane winds through houses toward a distant hill town.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The listening gathering evokes the teaching and proclamation in the synagogues. The grateful elderly man and supporting woman imaginatively suggest recipients of healing; the verse names no particular patient or family. The road and distant town recall travel through cities and villages. Jesus remains outside the picture, the unseen focus of the listeners. This is an illustrative setting, not a claim that these specific people or this moment are recorded.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of weary villagers beside stone houses: an elderly man sits bowed, a mother holds a sleeping child, and a crowd stretches along a dusty path. Three unaccompanied sheep stand or rest nearby, with flowers, trees and blue hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The exhausted villagers give imaginative form to the crowds Jesus saw with compassion. The nearby unaccompanied sheep echo the verse's comparison; the verse does not report a literal flock there. Jesus remains outside the frame. The setting and individual poses are imagined, and the warm light does not remove the people's weariness or need for a shepherd.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men in simple tunics harvest a vast golden wheat field. One bends with a curved sickle while the other kneels beside tied sheaves. Olive trees, a distant stone village and blue hills appear beneath a pale sky in a textured watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The broad expanse of ripe wheat and only two harvesters give visible form to the contrast Jesus states: a plentiful harvest and few workers. This is an imaginative illustration of His teaching, not a claim that the verse describes a literal harvesting scene. Jesus remains outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a man in a cream tunic and rust-colored mantle kneeling with open hands beneath an olive tree. Three robed workers walk along a path into golden wheat, one carrying a basket; a village and blue hills lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined harvest scene gives visible form to the verse's request: earnest prayer beside a field, with workers entering the grain. It illustrates the teaching rather than depicting a farming event narrated by the verse. The kneeling man is an ordinary petitioner; neither Jesus nor the Lord of the harvest is portrayed.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of two bearded men seated beside a limestone wall under an olive tree. The left man wears cream and ochre and looks upward; the right wears russet and blue-gray and lowers his gaze. Wildflowers, a hillside village and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative paired portrait represents Simon on the left and Judas on the right. Their appearances and hillside setting are not described in the verse. Judas's turned shoulders and lowered gaze recall the narrator's identification of his betrayal; no act of betrayal is depicted. Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four men in long cream tunics and earth-toned mantles stand in two pairs beside a blue lake. One rests an arm on his companion's shoulder. An olive tree frames the left; grasses, rocks, distant hills and stone houses surround the sunlit shore. Fine contours and textured watercolor washes give the scene a warm storybook appearance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two pairs imaginatively represent Simon Peter with Andrew, and James with John, reflecting the brother relationships named in the verse. Their appearance, clothing, gestures and lakeside setting are artistic choices; the verse supplies no portrait or location. Only the four men named here are shown, rather than the full twelve. Jesus is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six robed, bearded men converse in pairs in a sunlit stone courtyard beneath olive branches. A seated man in an ochre mantle is beside a small wooden table holding a dish of coins and a closed tablet. Olive trees, distant hills and small flowers surround the warm watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering represents the six names in their three textual pairs. The coin dish and closed tablet recall Matthew's designation as a tax collector; they do not depict a transaction. The verse supplies no scene, poses or likenesses. Jesus is outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed travelers walk along a rocky path toward villagers beside stone houses. Sheep stand scattered among olive trees, shrubs and flowers beneath a blue sky in a warm, detailed watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The travelers approaching the village imaginatively evoke the disciples going to Israel's people. Scattered sheep make the verse's metaphor visible; the instruction concerns people, not a literal flock. This landscape is an imaginative setting, not a recorded sheep-rescue episode. Jesus remains out of view.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of two robed travelers at a stone village doorway. One extends an open hand toward an older man, a smiling woman in a head covering, and a child. Olive branches, clay jars, wildflowers, and distant hills surround the sunlit path.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The traveling messengers and attentive household imaginatively illustrate going and proclaiming the nearness of the kingdom of heaven. The verse does not specify this village encounter or these listeners. Their hopeful attention suggests the reception of the announcement; the natural sunlight is atmosphere, not a depiction of God or a literal heavenly kingdom. Jesus remains out of view.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An open, empty brown leather money belt lies on a sunlit stone threshold beside gold-, silver-, and copper-colored coins. Clay vessels and olive branches frame a doorway overlooking an olive-lined path, a distant village, and hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life places an empty money belt beside three coins representing gold, silver, and copper. Keeping the coins outside the belt illustrates the command not to take money along; the road suggests departure. The verse does not describe this doorway or an incident of coins being left behind.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a kneeling man in an olive cloak supporting an elderly man seated on a woven mat beneath an ochre blanket. A standing man extends an open hand, while a woman in blue clasps her hands beside the stone doorway. Olive branches shade the sunlit courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined village encounter focuses on the command to heal and give freely: supportive hands and an empty open palm express help offered without payment. It does not depict a specific recorded miracle. Raising the dead, cleansing lepers, and casting out demons remain explicit commands in the verse, though not separately pictured. Jesus is outside the composition.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two barefoot men in cream and russet tunics receive a platter of bread and a bowl of food from a smiling older man at a sunlit stone doorway. An olive tree shades the courtyard, with a clay jug by the threshold and a village road behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household welcome illustrates the worker being worthy of food. The messengers wear single tunics and carry no provision-bags, sandals, spare clothing or staffs, reflecting the listed instructions. The particular host, meal and doorway are artistic choices, not an event specified by the verse. Jesus remains outside the view.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of two travelers listening to a seated gray-bearded villager who gestures toward a smiling householder at an open stone doorway. Woven sleeping mats and a clay jar sit inside. Grapevines shade the entrance, with an olive tree, flowers and village rooftops nearby.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined village encounter illustrates the instruction to inquire for a worthy host and stay there until departure. The neighbor directs the attentive travelers to a welcoming household; prepared sleeping mats suggest lodging. The verse does not identify this particular host or encounter. The welcome illustrates hospitality without claiming that appearance proves worthiness. Jesus remains outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed travelers approach an open stone doorway. One steps onto the threshold and raises a hand toward a bearded householder inside. Warm sunlight falls on pale stone, green leaves, a woven mat and an earthenware jar.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The unnamed travelers and householder imaginatively illustrate the command to greet a house upon entering. The raised hand and threshold make greeting and entry visible. The verse does not identify these people or describe their response.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed travelers greet a man and a head-covered woman at an open stone doorway. One traveler raises his hand, and the woman extends an open palm. Warm sunlight falls on the woven mat, clay jars, olive branches and village lane.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined welcome illustrates the worthy-house possibility in Matthew 10:13. The open threshold and attentive household suggest receiving the disciples' greeting of peace. Peace is conveyed through their calm expressions, not a visible force. The verse also commands their peace to return to them if the house is not worthy; that alternative is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed men stand outside a stone house with a closed wooden door. The nearer man raises one sandaled foot, shaking dust onto the path; his companion faces an olive-lined road leading toward a village and distant hills. Warm watercolor washes reveal textured paper, flowering grasses and rough stone.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined example illustrates the instruction to depart and shake dust from the feet when the disciples and their words are refused. The closed doorway suggests that refusal; the departing men and falling dust show the commanded response. The house, companions and landscape are artistic choices, not details of a particular event narrated here. Jesus remains out of view.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bronze balance stands on a stone ledge above an arid valley. Two ruined miniature cities sit in its raised left pan; an intact walled town with a closed wooden gate weighs down the right pan. Amber light breaks beneath blue-gray watercolor clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative balance illustrates the verse's comparison, not a scene described in Scripture. Two ruined city models evoke Sodom and Gomorrah; the closed-gate town sits lower to suggest the greater burden of judgment on the rejecting city. The scale is an artistic analogy, not an account of how final judgment occurs.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A small flock of sheep clusters on a rocky golden hillside as four wolves watch from surrounding ledges. Two pale doves perch on an olive branch in the foreground, opposite a brown serpent winding among sunlit stones. Blue hills and water lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined hillside gathers Jesus' three comparisons into one landscape: the exposed flock represents the disciples among hostile opposition; the alert serpent recalls prudence, and the doves recall innocence. The animals illustrate His teaching, not a recorded encounter or a depiction of Jesus. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a warm watercolor stone hall, a man in a blue tunic and pale mantle stands between two attendants before three seated council members. One attendant holds his mantle; the other gestures toward the council. A leather scourge rests on a cloth-covered stone bench in the foreground.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene anticipates the warning by showing a disciple brought before a council in a synagogue. The resting scourge indicates the threatened flogging without depicting an assault. The figures and arrangement are illustrative, not a named event or details specified by the verse. Jesus is outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men in worn robes stand before a seated official in white and a ruler wearing a gold circlet and red robes. One man extends an open hand as he speaks. An armored guard stands behind them, while listeners watch in a sunlit stone hall with columns and a distant hillside town.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined hearing pictures the testimony Jesus foretells: humble disciples brought before political rulers because of Him, with Gentile listeners present. The figures are unnamed; the verse does not specify a shared court, its architecture, or the outcome. Their sober posture conveys faithful witness under authority. Jesus is outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a cream robe and blue mantle speaking with one palm open before a seated official at a wooden table. An armed escort stands behind him beneath a stone arch; warm sunlight enters from a leafy courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined hearing gives visual form to being handed over and trusting that words will be given in that hour. The standing man represents an unnamed disciple beginning to answer without anxious rehearsal. The room, escort and official are illustrative details, not a particular event identified by this verse. Ordinary sunlight supports the hopeful mood; it does not portray God or promise release from the trial.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream tunic and rust-colored mantle speaks with an open hand in a sunlit stone courtyard. A companion stands behind him while three seated men listen. Olive branches shade the wall above a doorway, bench and clay water jug.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering illustrates the disciples speaking with quiet trust in the promise that their Father's Spirit speaks in them. It does not identify a particular recorded event. The Spirit remains unseen; the courtyard sunlight is ordinary light, not a depiction of God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of four robed men by a sunlit stone doorway. A rust-cloaked man extends an open hand toward a sorrowful man in olive, whose upper arm is held by a third man. A fourth waits beneath an arch; bread and two clay cups sit on a foreground table.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined handover focuses on a brother betraying his brother. The officials and the betrayed man's sorrow evoke the warning's mortal seriousness while the killing remains offstage. Bread and cups suggest family fellowship ruptured by betrayal. The courtyard and its details are imaginative; the verse also warns of fathers betraying children and children rising against parents, relationships not separately pictured here.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed disciples walk away along a sunlit stone lane while villagers on either side frown, turn away, raise a dismissive palm, and point them onward. Olive trees, warm stone houses, and a winding path lead toward pale hills under a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative village scene relates the villagers' rejection to hatred because of Jesus' name and the disciples' continuing steps to endurance. The warm light and onward path suggest hope in His promise that the one who endures to the end will be saved. The verse does not describe this particular event or promise an easy earthly escape; Jesus is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men in earth-colored robes hurry along a sunlit stone road away from a city gate, where small figures raise their arms. One man looks back while the other faces onward. Olive trees, flowers and golden hills surround the road leading toward another town.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined pair of disciples leaving a hostile city illustrates the command to flee to another rather than remain under persecution. The winding road and towns beyond suggest the continuing journey through Israel. The scene does not portray the Son of Man or assign a timetable to His coming; the exact people and landscape are imaginative.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of two robed men in a sunlit stone courtyard beneath grapevines. One sits on a woven stool holding a blank tablet; the other stands with a clay pitcher. Both look toward an open hand entering from the right above a wooden table. Olive trees and distant buildings appear beyond the wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard illustrates the verse's two relationships: a seated learner listens and a household servant waits with a pitcher, both attending to an unseen teacher or master. Their postures suggest subordinate roles; the verse does not narrate this scene. The hand is an indirect cue of instruction, not a portrait of Jesus or God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed men stand together in a sunlit stone doorway. The middle man rests a hand on the younger man's shoulder, while an older man bows his head. Beyond a low courtyard wall, two men point and jeer. Clay jars, woven cloth, green vines and an olive tree frame the warm watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household facing jeering neighbors illustrates the shared mistreatment Jesus describes: a disciple becomes like his teacher, and the household shares its master's reproach. The supportive hand suggests steadfast belonging amid slander. It is an illustrative setting, not an event narrated by this verse. Jesus is not depicted; Beelzebul is the malicious name used against the master, not his identity.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A reed basket of purple figs and a fig leaf rests on a sunlit stone ledge. A loose cream linen cloth lifts above the fruit and drapes over the rim. Olive and vine branches frame a limestone courtyard, with clay jars and village buildings beyond an open doorway.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard is an object illustration, not an event reported in the verse. Linen lifting from a basket makes concealed figs visible, echoing covered things being revealed and hidden things becoming known. The calm morning light accompanies the command not to fear; it does not promise an escape from suffering.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man in a sage tunic and russet mantle speaks with an outstretched hand from a sunlit stone rooftop. Men, women and a child look up from the lane. A dark stair doorway, clay jars and olive branches frame the warm watercolor village and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures a disciple carrying out Jesus' command to proclaim from the housetops. The shaded stair doorway beside the bright roof echoes the contrast between hearing in darkness and speaking in the light; it does not depict a separate recorded event or a visible whisper. Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A robed man stands with clasped hands on a rocky hillside at sunset. Armed men wait beside stone walls behind him, while fire and smoke rise from a deep ravine to the right. Olive branches frame the watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative landscape contrasts human persecutors, whose power is limited to bodily death, with a vast fiery ravine recalling Gehenna. The disciple's prayerful posture points to fear of God, who can destroy both soul and body; it does not promise bodily safety. This is a meditation on Jesus' warning, not a narrated event or a geographical depiction of hell. God and Jesus are not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two brown sparrows beside a woven basket in a sunlit stone village market: one perches on the rim, while the other lies on its side on the dusty ground with its eye closed. A copper coin rests on a foreground stone beneath olive branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined market scene pairs two sparrows and a copper coin to recall their small sale price. One bird lies still on the earth to acknowledge the verse's sober image of falling. The setting and the other bird's gaze are artistic choices; God remains unseen, and the scene does not promise freedom from death.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor rear view of a dark-haired man in a cream tunic and ochre wrap, seated beneath an olive tree with hands resting together. Fine sunlit hairs stand out against a landscape of wildflowers, a winding path, hillside houses and a blue lake.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Galilean listener is not a named biblical person. The close attention to individual hairs connects to Jesus' statement that every hair is numbered. The peaceful setting suggests the comfort of God's detailed knowledge; it does not portray a literal counting event or God in human form.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed men rest beneath an olive tree beside a low stone wall, one seated and one standing with a hand on his companion's shoulder. Brown sparrows perch, fly and peck among golden grasses and wildflowers, with a sunlit hillside village beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two listeners and many sparrows form an imaginative illustration of the verse's comparison, not a narrated encounter. Their relaxed faces suggest the reassurance of "do not fear," while the living birds recall those over whom Jesus declares His hearers' greater worth. Neither man represents Jesus; God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A short-haired man in an ochre tunic speaks with one hand on his chest and the other open toward five listeners in a sunlit stone courtyard. Olive branches hang overhead; pottery, flowers, distant hills and blue sky surround the gathering.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined disciple's open speech before villagers illustrates acknowledging Jesus before people. The spacious sky recalls Jesus' promise to acknowledge that person before His Father in heaven. The verse does not narrate this courtyard meeting; neither Jesus nor the Father is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a warm watercolor village courtyard, a troubled man in a cream tunic and rust mantle raises an open palm toward an empty path while addressing three sober listeners beside a stone doorway. Olive branches frame the pale blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard scene illustrates denying Jesus before people through the man's raised palm, turned posture and troubled exchange with witnesses. It does not claim a particular historical incident. Jesus remains outside the picture; the Father and heavenly judgment are not depicted. The verse's full warning remains that Jesus will also deny the denier before His Father in heaven.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an unsheathed sword resting diagonally across a sunlit stone threshold. Open wooden gates reveal a village lane and distant hills; a terracotta jar, leafy vine and small flowers frame the empty courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life does not depict a recorded event. The unheld sword crossing a threshold gives visible form to Jesus' warning that He came to bring not peace on earth, but a sword. Its dividing line suggests conflict attending His coming; the image does not portray Him wielding a weapon or command anyone to fight.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a young man stands apart from an older bearded man. Behind them, two women face each other at a doorway, while two more stand opposite one another beside clay jars. Downcast faces and folded arms suggest a household divided beneath olive branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined first-century household arranges the three relationships named in the verse as separated pairs: man and father, daughter and mother, daughter-in-law and mother-in-law. Their distance, lowered eyes and closed gestures illustrate the division Jesus says His coming brings. The verse does not record this particular gathering; Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a downcast man at a sunlit stone doorway facing an older man with folded arms and a woman turning away with her palm raised. Bread, cups, a clay jar and a woven basket sit on a wooden table in the modest home.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household scene relates the shared home to the verse's warning that a person's enemies can be those of his own household. The folded arms, rejecting palm and averted faces suggest hostility within domestic closeness. The particular people and incident are illustrative, not an event specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A sandaled traveler in an olive tunic and brown mantle carries a large, rope-bound wooden cross up a rocky hillside path. An olive tree, distant village, blue hills and small wildflowers surround him in warm watercolor light.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined disciple illustrates the costly following Jesus requires, rather than a recorded event. The heavy cross makes the demand tangible; the path continues beyond view toward the One he follows. Jesus is not depicted. The verse warns that a person who does not take his own cross and follow Him is not worthy of Him.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man in a cream tunic and ochre mantle steps onto a sunlit path, looking back with one hand over his chest. An elderly man and woman, a boy and a girl stand beside a stone doorway. An olive tree, wildflowers and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative family farewell illustrates the priority Jesus requires; the verse does not recount this event. The departing man represents a disciple, and Jesus remains outside the picture. His affectionate backward glance and deliberate onward step suggest the cost of following Jesus above parents or children, without treating his family as enemies.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A young man in a brown tunic and dusty blue mantle steps from a stone doorway onto a rocky hillside path. His hands hang open at his sides. Bread, pottery and a woven blanket remain inside; olive trees and wildflowers frame a distant village beneath a golden sunrise.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined disciple leaving a sheltered home for a rough road pictures surrender of self-preserving security for Jesus' sake. It is not an event narrated in the verse. Dawn suggests hope in His promise, without guaranteeing earthly safety or reducing losing one's life to travel. Jesus remains out of view. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling householder opens his arms to two travelers at a sunlit stone doorway. The men wear long tunics and earth-toned cloaks. Olive branches arch overhead; a clay jar stands beside the threshold, and a woven bench rests in the shaded room.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household welcome gives a visible setting to receiving the messengers Jesus addresses. The verse states that receiving them receives Jesus, and receiving Jesus receives the One who sent Him. It does not report this particular visit; neither Jesus nor the Father is pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a smiling host in ochre inviting two robed travelers into a vine-shaded stone courtyard. An older man holds a rolled scroll and staff; a younger man carries a cloth bundle. Bread, olives and a clay jug sit on a low wooden table, with woven chairs and distant hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard welcome illustrates receiving a prophet and a righteous person for who they are. The closed scroll distinguishes the prophet; the second traveler represents the righteous person. These are unnamed illustrative figures, not a recorded encounter. Hospitality makes reception visible, while the promised reward remains unseen rather than being reduced to money.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling woman in a terracotta dress and cream head covering offers a clay cup of water to a seated young man in a blue-gray tunic and brown mantle. A pitcher and small flowers stand beside the sunlit stone doorway, with olive branches overhead and hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined act of hospitality illustrates giving cold water to a humble disciple. The adult traveler represents one of the little ones without assuming that the phrase refers only to children. The village, host and encounter are illustrative details, not a recorded event. Jesus remains out of view; His assurance of reward is explained rather than pictured as material payment.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in long robes stand in a sunlit stone courtyard under an olive tree. The man in a rust-colored mantle holds one hand to his chest and extends the other palm upward toward the right. His companion stands behind with clasped hands; blue hills and village roofs appear beyond a low wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined questioner and companion embody the question addressed to Jesus: is He the Coming One, or should they expect another? Their open gesture and attentive faces convey an appeal awaiting a reply. Jesus remains outside the frame. The courtyard, clothing and exact arrangement are imaginative details, not claims supplied by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a brown robe sits behind an iron prison gate, raising an open hand toward two robed men. Warm daylight falls across stone walls, an earthen jar and a folded woven mat; a sunlit passage appears at right.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined visit represents John hearing of Christ's works and commissioning his disciples. Their faces, gestures, clothing and prison details are artistic choices. Two disciples form an illustrative group; the supplied Greek says 'through his disciples' and does not specify their number. Christ's works are conveyed as news rather than pictured. Jesus remains outside the scene.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in cream tunics and rust and olive mantles look attentively left. One carries a leather satchel. Pale stone houses, grape leaves, olive trees and a flower-lined path fill the sunlit watercolor village landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Their attentive gazes and the open path imaginatively connect hearing and seeing with the instruction to go and report to John. Jesus remains outside the picture. The two figures, courtyard, clothing and landscape are illustrative choices, not details specified by this verse; no particular miracle is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man steps through a sunlit stone courtyard beside a resting wooden crutch. An older seated man opens his hands, while three plainly dressed listeners look toward the right; one woman holds a hand near her ear. Olive branches, distant hills and clay jars frame the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering selects restored sight and walking, hearing, and the poor receiving good news from the verse's list. The crutch and listening gesture are visual cues, not details supplied by the text. Jesus remains outside the frame. The cleansing of lepers and raising of the dead are affirmed in the explanation but are not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a cream headcloth and terracotta robe seated beneath an olive tree. His hands rest on his knees and his sandaled feet are planted beside a stony path. He gazes upward to the right, with wildflowers, golden hills and distant stone houses around him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined listener receives the words of Jesus, who remains outside the frame, with quiet attention and trust. His settled posture and securely planted feet gently echo not stumbling. The verse concerns not taking offense at Jesus or falling away because of Him; the path is a visual analogy, not a claim that Jesus is a physical obstacle or that this scene is a recorded event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of robed listeners looking attentively to the right beside tall, wind-bent reeds and a rocky stream. Two travelers walk away along a winding path through dry golden hills beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The wind-bent reeds picture Jesus' rhetorical question, while attentive listeners and two departing travelers echo the verse. Jesus and John are not depicted. The stream and arrangement are imaginative; the verse does not place this speech beside these reeds or describe John as wavering.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in long burgundy and blue robes converse beneath sunlit stone arches. Cushions and fringed fabric cover a bench beside pottery and a gold-colored vessel; flowering vines, a mosaic floor and distant dry hills complete the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined royal household illustrates Jesus' example of people wearing soft garments in kings' houses. The anonymous figures, fine robes and sheltered arcade make that contrast tangible; the verse does not describe this particular conversation or palace. Jesus is outside the scene.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a coarse brown robe stands on a rock beside a stream, raising an open hand toward attentive, modestly robed listeners. Wildflowers line the stony path beneath a leafy tree and warm, distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined wilderness gathering recalls the people going out to see John the Baptist, whom Jesus affirms to be a prophet and more than a prophet. The listeners' attention connects the scene to that question. The river, clothing, poses and flowers are illustrative choices beyond the details stated in this verse. Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a coarse brown garment over a cream tunic walks along a sunlit, winding stone path, extending one hand toward the way ahead. An olive tree, rocks and small wildflowers frame golden hills beneath a pale blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The lone messenger represents John going ahead to prepare the way for Jesus, who remains outside the picture. The open wilderness path gives imaginative visible form to his preparatory ministry; the verse does not describe literal road construction. His clothing, gesture and landscape are illustrative details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a rough brown mantle stands beside a river with open hands, while a man in a patched robe walks beneath a flower-covered stone arch toward a sunlit garden. Olive branches, reeds, distant hills and small wildflowers surround the path.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative meditation, not a recorded meeting: the honored John stands by the river, while an anonymous humble person approaching the radiant garden represents even the least in the kingdom. The open arch and continuous path suggest the kingdom's greater standing without depicting John as rejected. The garden is an artistic metaphor, not a description of heaven; greatness is not physical size.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of three robed men bracing against a partly opened wooden gate in a sunlit limestone arch. One pushes the planks, another presses behind him, and a third grips the door edge. Through the gap are a stone path, flowers and an olive tree; a hillside village lies beyond the wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The pressured doorway is an imaginative metaphor for the verse's violence and grasping, not a recorded siege or a literal entrance to heaven. The men straining at the wood echo the supplied passive reading, 'is taken by violence.' Quiet light beyond suggests the kingdom's preciousness without portraying God or Jesus. The image does not teach that violence earns entry.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a large open blank parchment scroll and several rolled scrolls on a wooden table beneath a rocky overhang. Beyond them, a bearded man in a shaggy brown cloak raises one hand beside a reed-lined river, with flowers, olive branches and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The scrolls imaginatively represent the Law and the collective witness of the prophets; their arrangement leads the eye toward John beside the river, recalling that they prophesied until John. This symbolic juxtaposition is not a recorded meeting or an event described in the verse. Jesus is outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle sits beneath an olive tree, cupping a hand behind one ear and looking up to the right. Wildflowers, a sunlit path, olive groves, distant hills and pale village buildings surround him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The attentive listener illustrates the verse's call to hear. His cupped hand and receptive expression make listening visible. The hillside, clothing and individual are imaginative setting details, not an event or person named in this verse. Jesus remains outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a coarse brown outer garment stands beside a river, extending one hand toward a seated man and woman in modest robes. Reeds, rocks, leafy branches and sunlit hills surround them in a warm watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined riverside scene represents John the Baptist's prophetic ministry; the listeners' open hands evoke willingness to receive Jesus' teaching. Matthew 11:14 identifies John as the promised Elijah who was to come. The setting and gestures are artistic additions, not events stated in this verse; no meeting with Elijah or depiction of Jesus is intended.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five children in long robes sit facing one another on stone steps in a sunlit marketplace. A child cups a hand beside an open mouth while another reaches toward the opposite pair. Fruit baskets, clay jars, cloth awnings and flowering vines surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The seated children calling across the marketplace give visible form to Jesus' comparison. Their faces, clothing and market surroundings are imaginative details, not a claim that this was a recorded event. The scene stays with this verse without adding the games described afterward.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a rough brown cloak stands empty-handed on a sunny stone path. Behind him, three robed villagers whisper and point from a shaded doorway. Bread and a clay cup rest untouched on a stone ledge beside flowers and an olive tree, with hills and village houses beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined village-edge encounter represents John's abstinent life through his empty hands and untouched bread and cup. The villagers' whispering and pointing stand for the accusation that he has a demon. No demon is depicted, because the verse reports their accusation rather than affirming it. The location, people and meal arrangement are illustrative, not details supplied by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Coarse brown sackcloth hangs over a low stone seat beside a clay bowl of gray ashes. Olive branches and pottery frame a sunlit arch overlooking blue harbor water, wooden boats and pale coastal houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life uses sackcloth and ashes to evoke the repentance Jesus says Tyre and Sidon would have shown. The coastal setting recalls those cities without claiming an exact location or an event that occurred. The verse's woe against Chorazin and Bethsaida remains a warning about their response to His mighty works.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed men smile as bread is passed across a courtyard table set with flatbread, olives, clay cups and a pitcher. A coin pouch and a few coins rest at the left. Two frowning men confer in the shaded doorway behind them, beneath warm stone walls and olive branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard meal evokes fellowship with tax collectors and sinners; the coin pouch hints at that social setting. Jesus remains outside the picture. The disapproving onlookers recall the accusations against Him, while shared bread and welcome suggest wisdom recognized by her deeds. The verse does not identify this particular meal or these guests.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a sunlit stone town. A bearded man stands with folded arms, another walks away down the lane, and a veiled woman turns toward a doorway. A rolled woven mat rests on a step beneath leafy branches; olive trees and distant hillside houses fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Galilean street uses turned backs, averted faces and folded arms to suggest the cities' refusal to repent. The rolled mat is an artistic reminder of past works of mercy, not a detail supplied by the verse. Jesus' rebuke is represented indirectly; He is outside the frame. No particular miracle or subsequent judgment is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bronze balance on a limestone ledge above a blue sea. Two small coastal town models and a few stones occupy the higher left pan; one town model and larger stones fill the lower right pan. An olive branch rests beside the base under a softly clouded sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This is an imaginative visual analogy, not an event described in the verse. The two coastal town models in the raised pan stand for Tyre and Sidon; the single town and heavier stones in the lowered pan stand for the hearers' greater judgment. Both pans carry stones, preserving the comparison of severity rather than suggesting exemption. The balance and models are artistic devices; God and Jesus are not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bronze balance stands on a stone slab in a warm, rocky landscape. Its raised left pan holds ruined buildings; its lower right pan holds an intact miniature stone town. A winding path, trees, distant hills and violet clouds surround it.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The balance and miniature towns are an imaginative comparison, not objects or an event described in the verse. The raised ruined settlement evokes Sodom; the lower, heavier intact town evokes the place Jesus warns. The unequal pans express more tolerable versus more severe judgment, without suggesting that Sodom escapes judgment.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A sunlit stone town beside a blue lake rises behind a ruined gateway. Worn steps curve down into a deep, dark rocky cleft. Olive trees, dry golden grasses, scattered carved stones and distant purple hills surround the scene beneath a cloud-filled sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The downward stair and dark cleft symbolize Capernaum's threatened descent to Hades; the ruined stones recall Sodom, which Jesus says would have remained had it received the same mighty works.
