This is an imaginative comparison, not literal geography or a claim that Capernaum was destroyed in this manner. Jesus and particular miracles are left unseen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two young children in cream and terracotta robes sit on a woven mat, smiling upward attentively. Behind them, two robed men study a blank scroll beneath an olive tree. The sunlit stone courtyard overlooks golden hills and a village beneath a blue sky with soft clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative courtyard contrasts the children's receptive wonder in sunlight with learned adults studying in shade, reflecting the Father's revealing and hiding in Jesus' praise. The verse does not narrate this gathering or identify these things as the scroll. Jesus stays outside the frame; the Father is not depicted. Sky and earth recall His lordship over both. The contrast does not condemn learning.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two open hands in cream linen sleeves face upward above a rocky hillside path. An old olive tree, wildflowers and low stone walls frame distant hills and a small village beneath a warm blue-and-gold sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The praying hands imaginatively suggest Jesus' willing yes to the Father's good pleasure while keeping Him otherwise out of view. The quiet hillside supports reverent assent; neither this setting nor the gesture is specified by the verse. The natural sky does not depict the Father.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed listeners sit beside a stone archway as a hand draws back a golden curtain, revealing a sunlit garden with an olive tree, red and yellow flowers, and a winding path.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined doorway scene illustrates disclosure, not an event reported in the verse. The unseen curtain-drawer's hand suggests the Son revealing the Father to those He chooses. The garden and sunlight evoke received understanding; they do not depict the Father or express the whole mystery of the Father and Son's mutual knowledge.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Under sunlit olive trees, an older man in ochre and a woman in green rest beside a rope-tied bundle and woven basket. Both look upward to the right. A third traveler approaches carrying a load; pale hills and a distant village lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: These imagined travelers and their lowered loads illustrate the weary and burdened whom Jesus invites to Himself. Their shared gaze suggests His invitation beyond the frame; He is not depicted. Physical loads visualize weariness and the promise of rest without claiming that the verse recounts this particular scene or limits His rest to relief from manual labor.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A wooden yoke with two curved bows rests on sunlit limestone beneath an olive tree. An empty stone bench and terracotta jug stand nearby, while a winding path leads through fields toward distant hills and a village.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Galilean resting place uses the intact yoke to picture accepting Jesus' teaching, while the shaded seat and peaceful path suggest His promised rest for souls. The verse does not describe this location or these objects as a historical scene. Jesus is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A honey-brown wooden double yoke and a woven basket holding cream linen rest on a pale stone bench. Olive branches shade a sunlit courtyard, with wildflowers, a clay jar, a winding path, cultivated fields and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The intact yoke and modest basket imaginatively pair the verse's two images. Their peaceful setting evokes the ease and lightness Jesus describes. The courtyard is an illustrative composition, not an event recorded in the verse; no figure represents Jesus.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded travelers in cream, russet, green and ochre robes rest beneath an olive tree. The central man extends an open hand above an empty leather bag and earthenware bowl. Rocky hills and a distant village lie behind them in warm sunlight.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined pause represents David and his hungry companions, whom Jesus recalls in His question. The empty bag and bowl make their hunger visible; the resting place, clothing and number of companions are artistic choices, not details stated in this verse. Jesus remains out of view, and the bread episode is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four robed men stand on a stone-lined path beside golden grain. At left, one man extends an open hand toward someone beyond the frame while his companion folds his arms. At right, two men hold grain heads and kernels. Olive branches, wildflowers and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two men at left represent Pharisees objecting to Jesus about His disciples, represented at right. Jesus remains outside the frame. The grainfield, grain in their hands, gestures and landscape are imaginative setting details; this verse itself records the Sabbath accusation without describing the disciples' activity or Jesus' reply.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a robed traveler breaking a round loaf beside a cloth-covered wooden table with bread on a golden tray. An ivory-robed priest stands nearby while two men eat bread beneath a woven doorway curtain. Hills and olive trees lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The sacred loaves and priest evoke the bread of the Presence, reserved for priests, while the travelers eating recall the event described in the verse. The sanctuary doorway, clothing, tray and two visible companions are imaginative choices; the verse does not specify their appearance or number.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed listeners, two bearded men and a woman in a blue mantle, look attentively toward the upper right beneath an olive tree. Sunlight warms their cream garments, limestone terrace and small purple flowers. Across the valley stands a pale stone temple complex with golden details under a soft blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The distant temple and nearby listeners imaginatively juxtapose the temple's honored grandeur with Jesus' declaration that something greater is here. The listeners attend to Him beyond the frame; He is not pictured. The terrace overlooking the temple is an artistic setting, not a location stated by this verse. Warm sunlight conveys attentive wonder rather than a depicted supernatural event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in ivory robes and linen head coverings serve in a sunlit stone temple courtyard. One lays wood on a burning horned bronze altar; the others carry firewood and a bronze bowl. A rolled scroll rests on a foreground stone ledge.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative courtyard shows priests tending an altar, carrying wood and holding a service bowl. Their willing labor pictures the Sabbath service Jesus cites; their calm expressions suggest guiltlessness without denying His word 'profane.' The rolled scroll alludes to His appeal to the Law. The verse does not specify these particular tasks, people or architecture. Jesus is outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A traveler in olive robes places bread into the cupped hands of a seated traveler in blue beside a golden grain field. A clay water jug and cut grain rest nearby; an altar with a small flame in its bowl stands behind them among olive trees and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: These imagined travelers are not a recorded incident from the verse. Sharing bread pictures mercy, while the background altar recalls the mention of sacrifice. The seated traveler's dignified treatment invites reflection on Jesus' rebuke against condemning the guiltless. Neither traveler represents Jesus.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men and a woman in modest robes sit beneath an olive tree beside a stone wall, looking attentively toward the upper left. A basket, folded cloth and unused hoe rest nearby. Golden grain, village houses and blue hills fill the sunlit background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Sabbath setting pairs an unused work tool and resting listeners with attentive faces turned toward a speaker outside the picture. Their listening suggests recognition of the Son of Man's authority over the Sabbath. The verse states that authority; it does not describe these people, objects or this gathering. Jesus is kept outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a sunlit stone synagogue doorway beneath olive branches. A worn path leads across the threshold to a wooden stand with a rolled scroll. Two robed men sit on stone benches inside; village buildings and hills appear to the left.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The path and open synagogue doorway imagine the destination of Jesus' movement in Matthew 12:9 while keeping Him outside the visible scene. The stone building, olive tree, scroll and two seated worshippers are illustrative setting details that the verse does not specify. The image does not depict a healing or another subsequent event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a seated man in cream robes and a blue mantle, supporting the wrist of his thin, curled hand. Three robed men stand behind him; one gestures with an open palm toward the right. Sunlight enters the stone room through an opening overlooking distant hills and buildings.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The seated pose, stone room, clothing and gestures are imaginative staging for the man with a withered hand and the question asked to accuse Jesus. The standing men direct their attention beyond the frame, keeping Jesus unseen. The hand remains contracted: this illustrates the question about Sabbath healing, without depicting the later healing.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two hands in rolled linen sleeves support a cream-colored sheep as it rises from a rocky earthen pit, its front hooves reaching the rim. Olive trees, wildflowers, distant stone houses and sunlit hills surround the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures the hypothetical rescue in Jesus' question, not a separately reported event. One sheep, the visible pit and the owner's supporting hands connect directly to taking hold and lifting it out. The peaceful hillside supplies an imagined setting; it does not visibly establish a Sabbath. Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a younger man in ochre and blue offers a clay cup to a seated elder in olive and cream, resting a hand on his shoulder. A cream-colored sheep lies beside their bench beneath olive branches, with hills and village houses beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined act of offering water illustrates doing good and honoring human worth; the resting sheep recalls the verse's explicit comparison. This courtyard encounter is illustrative, not an event narrated in the verse or a depicted healing. Both men are unnamed neighbors, and Jesus is outside the composition.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a smiling bearded man in an olive tunic, cream striped mantle and cloth cap. He extends an open hand toward the left while looking at it; his other hand rests open near his waist. A stone bench and softly lit plaster and stone walls stand behind him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The extended, healthy hand pictures the restoration after the man obeys Jesus; his other open hand echoes the verse's comparison. Jesus remains outside the frame. The man's expression, clothing and simple stone interior are imaginative staging, not details specified by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four bearded men in earth-colored robes and striped head coverings huddle beside an open stone doorway. One gestures while the others listen with furrowed brows. Sunlit paving, flowering plants, olive branches and distant hills surround them in warm watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The close, tense council imagines the Pharisees taking counsel against Jesus with the intention of destroying him. The four figures, their gestures and the stone courtyard are illustrative details, not details specified by the verse. Jesus remains outside the frame. No assault is shown: the verse describes their murderous planning.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling crowd in long robes walks along a sunlit, olive-lined path. An elderly man holds his hands over his heart beside a woman in an ochre shawl; a mother rests her hand on a smiling boy. Stone village houses and blue hills rise behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined countryside procession pictures the many who followed Jesus and the gratitude of those He healed. Jesus remains beyond the bend, outside the frame; no visible person is the healer. The olive grove, village, individual people and their gestures are artistic details, not particulars supplied by the verse. The image suggests the outcome of His healing rather than reconstructing how each cure occurred.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three adults in earth-toned robes stand beneath an olive tree, looking attentively to the left. A woman holds a hand to her chest; the men keep their hands lowered. A stone wall, wildflowers, village houses and lavender hills fill the sunlit landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The quiet listeners imaginatively evoke those receiving Jesus' firm warning not to make Him known. Jesus stays outside the frame. Their number, clothing, gestures and hillside setting are artistic choices, not details stated in the verse; their attentive silence suggests the restraint His instruction requires.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An unmarked parchment scroll with wooden rollers rests on a sunlit stone ledge beside a reed pen and ink cup. An earthenware jug holds olive branches at left. A stone arch frames a flower-lined path through olive trees toward blue hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life uses the scroll to recall the word spoken through Isaiah. The sunlight and continuing path suggest fulfillment. Matthew 12:17 does not describe this setting or these objects; the unmarked parchment avoids inventing the prophecy's wording.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A warm watercolor of a quiet stone village street. Grapevines shade a wooden doorway beside clay jars and a woven basket. A woman in a terracotta robe and cream head covering walks with a child in blue; olive trees, flowers and hillside houses fill the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined village street reflects the verse through its open space and absence of quarrelling or public outcry. The ordinary villagers are artistic additions. Jesus remains outside the picture; this is a meditation on His uncontentious manner, not a recorded incident or a claim that He never spoke publicly.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five attentive listeners in blue, rust, ochre, sage and rose robes gather beneath an olive tree on a stone terrace. A mother rests her hands on a girl's shoulders. Clay vessels and flowers sit nearby; a sailboat, blue water and a distant hillside town fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The varied listeners imagine the nations receiving the chosen servant's proclamation of justice. This harbor gathering is an imaginative setting, not a meeting reported in the verse. Jesus remains outside the frame; God's delight and the gift of His Spirit are affirmed by the text rather than depicted as visible beings.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bruised green reed rises from shallow lake water beside a clay oil lamp on a stone ledge. Its wick glows faintly and sends up a thin curl of smoke. Golden dawn lights distant hills and a small stone house in a textured watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined lakeshore still life brings together the verse's bruised reed and smoldering flax wick, preserved rather than destroyed. It pictures Christ's gentleness without portraying Him. The dawn suggests hope; it does not literally depict His bringing justice to victory.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six travelers in layered robes gather beneath an olive tree above a sunlit harbor. An elderly man rests his hands on a staff, a woman keeps a hand on a child's shoulder, and all look expectantly toward the upper right. Wildflowers line the stone path; sailboats and pale buildings lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering of Gentile travelers pictures the nations' promised hope in Jesus. Their shared gaze is directed beyond the right edge, leaving Him unseen. The harbor suggests different homelands; the verse does not describe this particular gathering, landscape, or clothing. Daylight is ordinary illumination, not a substitute for Him.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a seated, bearded man in an ochre tunic and blue mantle, looking upward with open eyes and parted lips. One hand touches his chest and the other opens outward. Two smiling men in olive and russet clothing accompany him beside warm stonework, olive branches and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene concentrates on the man's restored sight and speech after Jesus heals him. Jesus remains outside the frame. The courtyard, clothing and companions' gestures are imagined details, not specified by the verse. Demon possession is part of the verse's account, acknowledged in the explanation without inventing a visible spirit or ritual.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a crowd in a sunlit stone village. Seven foreground men and women in earth-colored robes show astonishment with open palms and lifted faces, while two men turn toward each other in questioning conversation. More villagers gather behind them beneath olive branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The crowd's amazed faces and the two neighbors' questioning exchange imaginatively express the verse's astonishment and question about the Son of David. Jesus remains outside the frame as the unseen focus. The courtyard, clothing, gestures and individual faces are artistic choices, not details specified by this verse; the picture does not turn their question into a coronation or formal declaration.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in cream head coverings and earth-toned robes gather in a sunlit stone courtyard. One speaks with an outstretched hand while the others lean close, one resting his hand against his beard. Olive branches hang overhead beside a clay jar and stone bench.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The three speakers imaginatively represent the Pharisees making their accusation. Their tense discussion and outward gesture evoke speech about Jesus, who remains outside the frame. The courtyard and exact poses are reconstructed details. No demons appear: the verse records the charge that He works by Beelzebul, rather than a visible demonic event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor model of a walled stone city sits on a wooden table. A deep crack splits its earthen base and central arch, with loose blocks below and matching burgundy pennants above. Olive branches, pottery and sunlit hills surround it.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This is an imaginative teaching model, not a recorded event. Its single kingdom, broken through its own foundation, illustrates Jesus' conditional argument: if Satan casts out Satan, his kingdom is divided against itself and cannot stand. No figure represents Jesus, God or Satan.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six adults in long robes dispute on opposite sides of a courtyard beside a limestone home with a collapsed central roof and scattered masonry. An olive tree, pottery and baskets frame the scene; a winding lane leads toward a partly ruined walled town beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The divided household beside its broken shared home and the ruined town imaginatively picture Jesus' warning that internal division brings desolation and prevents a kingdom, city or household from standing. The verse does not narrate this building collapse; the architecture is a visual analogy, and Jesus remains out of view.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four robed men, two older and two younger, consider one another beside a bronze balance holding equal pale stones in a sunlit stone courtyard. An olive tree arches overhead, with warm village buildings beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The courtyard gathering and balance are imaginative, not details stated in the verse. The equal stones suggest applying the same standard to Jesus and the accusers' own exorcists. The younger men evoke the sons or followers whose work challenges the accusation. Jesus is not depicted, and no exorcism is staged.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed adults look upward in a sunlit stone courtyard. A seated man opens his hands; two companions watch beside him. Olive branches, a clay jar and flowers surround them, and violet wisps curl beyond an open doorway.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The courtyard and people are imaginative, not details specified by the verse. The central man represents someone delivered, not Jesus; departing violet wisps suggest expelled demons. Ordinary daylight and grateful witnesses evoke God's reign already arriving. Jesus remains outside the frame; the Spirit is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor stone-house interior shows a bearded man in a long olive tunic, tied to a wooden chair with his wrists bound in his lap. At the sunlit doorway, two hands lift a woven basket of clay vessels and folded cloth. An open wooden chest, jars, baskets, and a striped rug furnish the room.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household illustrates Jesus' comparison, rather than a recorded burglary or a portrayal of Jesus. The restrained strong man and the goods being carried away express the sequence He states: first bind the strong man, then plunder his house. The setting and household details are artistic choices.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A green-robed worker binds a golden wheat sheaf beside a basket beneath an olive tree. A russet-robed worker walks away, dropping cut wheat onto a stony path, with fields, hills and pale village buildings beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined harvest contrasts a worker binding wheat with another walking away and letting cut stalks fall apart. It illustrates Jesus' opposition between gathering with Him and scattering, rather than documenting an event in the verse. Neither worker portrays Jesus.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four adults in olive, ochre, terracotta and blue robes listen intently toward the right beneath an olive tree in a sunlit stone courtyard. An elderly man and a cream-veiled woman sit together; a younger man holds a hand to his chest, and a blue-veiled woman stands behind. A clay jug, small flowers and distant hills complete the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined group listens to Jesus outside the frame. Their sober attention reflects both the promise that sin and blasphemy will be forgiven and the grave exception: blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven. The courtyard and gestures are artistic inventions, not details given by this verse, and no listener is identified as guilty of that sin. The Spirit is not visually represented.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed adults sit beneath an olive tree in a sunlit stone courtyard. A woman cups her hands, a dark-haired man holds one hand near his lips and one palm open, and an older man rests folded arms over his knee. Flowers, an earthenware jug and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering of listeners invites reflection on Jesus' solemn distinction between forgiveness for a word against the Son of Man and no forgiveness for speaking against the Holy Spirit, in this age or the coming age. The hand near the lips recalls the weight of speech; open and folded hands suggest differing responses. The verse does not describe this courtyard or these people, and the image assigns no one a verdict. Jesus and the Holy Spirit remain unseen. Human artwork review is pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor orchard with a leafy fig tree bearing plump purple and green fruit beside a hollow, decaying tree with curled leaves and shriveled dark figs. Fallen spoiled fruit lies near its roots; a sunlit path leads toward a stone wall and golden hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two fig trees are an imaginative illustration of Jesus' comparison, not a recorded orchard visit. Sound fruit and spoiled fruit make each tree's condition visible. The verse does not specify a fruit species or setting.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A tipped terracotta jug pours muddy water into a stone channel. Three brown patterned vipers rest among rocks beside it. Olive branches, warm limestone walls, an arched doorway and flowers frame the sunlit courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The jug's dark contents pouring through its mouth imaginatively connect the heart's abundance to spoken words. Three vipers recall Jesus' sharp address, offspring of vipers. This is a symbolic still life, not a recorded courtyard event. No figure represents Jesus or God. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two open wooden chests sit on a sunlit stone ledge. One holds bread, grapes, figs and wheat spilling onto linen; the other holds thorn branches and spoiled fruit. Olive leaves shade the courtyard, and an arch frames distant hills and village houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative still life, not a recorded event: the two stores picture the good and evil treasure in the verse. Wholesome provisions and harmful thorns with spoiled fruit show how what comes forth corresponds to what is stored within. The objects are metaphors for moral character, not a claim that food or possessions determine goodness.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in cream clothing and a terracotta mantle sits with one hand against his mouth beside a blank parchment, three stones and a bronze balance. Flowers, olive branches, stone walls and distant hills surround the sunlit courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined listener reflects on his speech. The blank scroll, stones and balance are illustrative metaphors for giving account of every careless word on judgment day; the verse describes neither these objects nor this courtyard. The man is not Jesus, and no final-judgment event is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bronze balance holds a tied papyrus scroll in each pan on a stone table. A blank unrolled sheet and reed pen lie in front. Warm light and cool shadow cross the courtyard, with olive branches, a clay jug, a stone arch and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life is not an event described in the verse. The scrolls stand for a person's own words, and the scales recall the verdicts of justification and condemnation. Light and shadow emphasize those contrasting outcomes; they neither depict God nor imply that good words cancel evil words.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed men stand in a sunlit stone courtyard. One extends an open palm toward the left, while the others watch in that direction; the man at right holds a rolled scroll. Olive branches, clay jars and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard scene visualizes the scribes and Pharisees asking their unseen Teacher for a sign. Their attentive faces and open hand express the request; Jesus remains outside the frame. The verse does not name the location, clothing or number of speakers, and no sign is shown as having occurred.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a long cream robe and rust-colored mantle stands on a sunlit rocky shore, head bowed and hand at his chest. A great fish's back and tail break the blue-green water beyond him; low headlands and a warm clouded sky fill the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative shore scene evokes Jonah, the prophet Jesus names as the sole sign. The shore and departing fish recall Jonah's story; they are not details narrated in Matthew 12:39 or a depiction of Jesus' audience. The humbled posture is an artistic choice. The verse rebukes an evil and adulterous generation for seeking a sign.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A whale-like sea creature swims beneath turquoise water beside a rocky coast. A round stone closes a tomb in the ochre cliff. An olive tree and shrubs grow above, while a pale moon hangs over a rose-and-gold twilight sea.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative coastal pairing compares the creature that held Jonah with a closed tomb recalling the Son of Man in the heart of the earth. Their shared shoreline is an artistic comparison, not a historical claim. Twilight suggests waiting without attempting to count or shorten the three days and three nights. Neither Jonah nor Jesus is shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor of a robed messenger seen from behind addressing men beneath an ochre city gate. A man in rough sackcloth kneels with his head bowed and a hand over his chest; an older man stands with lowered eyes and open palms. Other listeners gather around them, with sunlit city buildings beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative view of Jonah preaching in Nineveh illustrates the repentance Jesus cites as grounds for the Ninevites' future condemnation of His generation at the judgment. The architecture, faces and gestures are artistic choices. It does not depict the future judgment or Jesus, the One greater than Jonah whose presence makes the comparison so solemn.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A veiled queen in an ochre robe and teal mantle listens to a crowned king seated in a sunlit stone courtyard. Attendants stand behind her, and two laden camels follow a winding road through dry hills. Olive branches, flowering vines, pottery and woven cloth frame the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined visit recalls the queen's journey to hear Solomon, the reason Jesus gives for her condemnation of this generation at judgment. The courtyard, clothing and caravan are artistic details. Jesus and the future judgment remain outside the picture; the verse declares that One greater than Solomon is here.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a barren rocky ravine, with cracked earth, thorn bushes, ochre cliffs and lavender hills beneath a pale sky. A small charcoal-gray wisp curls above the dry channel. No people are visible.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined waterless ravine illustrates the spirit's fruitless search for rest. The dark wisp is an artistic suggestion of the unclean spirit, not a claim about its visible form. Its departure from the person is outside the composition, and no later return is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An open wooden door reveals an empty stone-and-plaster room with a clean earthen floor. Sunlight falls beside a reed broom; clay jars, folded cloths, a basket, and a rolled mat are neatly arranged beneath timber rafters.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined ancient house visualizes the verse's house imagery rather than a documented building. The clean floor, broom, and arranged vessels show it swept and put in order; the vacant center emphasizes that it is unoccupied. The returning speaker remains unseen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a sunlit stone house with an open wooden door and a dark violet interior. Pale gray and darker purple streams curl across the dusty lane into the doorway. A clay jar stands beside the steps; olive branches, village houses and blue hills surround the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The house is an imaginative metaphor for the man, not a separate event asserted by the verse. The lighter wisp and gathering darker streams evoke the returning spirit and seven more wicked companions dwelling there, making his condition worse. The nearby village extends the image toward Jesus' warning about this evil generation. The shadows do not claim to show spirits' actual appearance.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A veiled woman and four robed men stand outside a sunlit stone house. One man extends an open hand toward a doorway, where seated listeners face farther into a shaded room. Olive branches frame the warm watercolor scene, and a clay jar rests by the threshold.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The waiting woman and men imaginatively represent Jesus' mother and brothers, and the shaded gathering recalls the crowds He was still addressing. Jesus remains out of view. The house, gestures, clothing and appearances are illustrative; the verse does not specify these details or explain why His family wished to speak.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man inside an open wooden doorway gesturing toward a gray-haired woman in a blue shawl and two men standing in a sunlit stone courtyard, with olive branches, vines, clay jars and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The messenger's open hand connects his report to the mother and brothers standing outside. The doorway, clothing, expressions and two representative brothers are imaginative staging, not details specified by the verse. Jesus remains outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six robed adults sit closely inside a sunlit stone house, looking toward the upper left. A bearded man in a blue shawl rests a hand at his chin; an older woman wears a cream head covering. Olive branches and clay jars frame the warm watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The listening group imagines the pause after Jesus asks who His mother and brothers are. Jesus remains outside the frame; the central man represents the person He answers. The older woman and other adults evoke family without claiming to identify His relatives. The setting and expressions are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Seven robed men sit closely on woven mats beside a sunlit stone doorway, looking toward an open hand entering from the lower left. Leafy branches shade the warm watercolor scene; clay vessels and distant houses complete the setting.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The open hand represents Jesus' gesture toward His disciples, while His face and body remain outside the image. Their close grouping evokes His words calling them His mother and brothers. The number, faces, clothing, house and light are imaginative setting details, not details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Under an olive tree in a sunlit stone courtyard, a young woman touches an older woman's arm while a kneeling young man offers the older woman a clay cup. All wear modest robes, with soft hills visible beyond the courtyard wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative gathering uses caring fellowship among ordinary disciples to evoke the brother, sister and mother relationship Jesus names for whoever does His heavenly Father's will. The courtyard and offered water are artistic choices, not details narrated in this verse. Jesus and the heavenly Father are not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A farmer seen from behind, wearing a cream tunic, russet cloak and headcloth, scatters golden grain from a woven seed bag into a brown worked field. An olive tree and stone wall edge the path; distant hills, olive trees and small buildings sit beneath a blue, clouded sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The farmer is an imagined figure within the parable Jesus begins, not a depiction of Jesus. His step toward the field and scattering grain picture the sower going out to sow. The clothing and landscape are illustrative details, not facts supplied by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor view over a wooden boat's bow, with rope, netting and a basket, toward a large standing crowd in earth-toned robes on a pebbled lakeshore. Blue-green water, a leafy tree, distant houses and sunlit hills surround the gathering.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined viewpoint from inside the boat links its wooden bow to the crowd standing on shore, as the verse describes. Jesus, who entered the boat and sat down, remains outside the painted view. The attentive faces, garments, tree, distant houses and fishing gear are illustrative details, not additional claims made by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five brown birds gather over scattered grain on a sunlit dirt path, several pecking and one alighting. A linen-sleeved hand drops seed from the upper left. Tilled soil, wildflowers, olive trees and distant hills surround the path.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined close view makes the verse's action visible: seed falls beside the path and birds eat it. The cropped hand represents the parable's anonymous sower. The countryside and individual bird details are artistic choices; no portrait of Jesus or additional symbolic interpretation is intended.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Fresh green seedlings and golden grains lie in thin brown soil above pale rock, with fine roots exposed along its edge. Olive trees, white flowers, a distant village and blue hills fill the sunlit watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined close view illustrates seed springing up in shallow earth over rock. The exposed ledge and visible roots make the lack of soil depth apparent; the hillside and distant village supply an imagined setting. The fresh shoots depict early growth, without adding the following verse's withering.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of drooping, yellowing grain shoots surrounded and overshadowed by tall, spiny green plants, with scattered seeds and stones on ochre soil and pale hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined field-margin view illustrates the seed among thorns by showing weak grain shoots overtopped and crowded by thorn growth. The particular plants, scattered seeds, terrain and distant hills are artistic details, not specifics named in the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Curled ochre and faded green shoots droop from cracked, shallow soil over pale rock. A bright sun hangs above lavender hills, with scattered stones and yellow-flowering shrubs in the warm watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined stony ledge suggests the lack of an established root through a thin skin of soil above rock. Curled, drying shoots beneath the risen sun illustrate the verse's sequence of scorching and withering. The landscape details are an artistic setting, not additional events stated in the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Golden wheat with heavy, bending heads grows in brown soil. Scattered kernels lie in the foreground, while the sunlit field stretches toward low hills beneath a blue sky with soft white clouds. Fine contours and textured watercolor washes define the grain.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative harvest landscape depicts the fruitful outcome of seed falling on good soil. Differences in the fullness and density of the wheat suggest the differing yields; the image does not count the hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold returns. The scattered kernels connect the harvest to seed. Jesus is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in cream robes and a rust-colored shawl, seated among stones and wildflowers with one hand cupped behind his ear. A woman in olive and cream sits behind him beneath an olive tree; blue hills fade in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined hillside scene expresses the verse's call to hear through an ordinary listener's cupped ear and attentive posture. The verse does not specify these people, their gestures, or this landscape; the speaker stays outside the frame.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four bearded men in earth-colored robes gather beneath a leafy tree on a rocky lakeshore, looking beyond the right edge. The foremost man holds one palm open. A seated crowd, blue water, a small sailboat, distant village and hills appear behind them in warm, finely outlined watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The four foreground men imaginatively represent disciples who have drawn near to ask Jesus why He speaks in parables. Their gaze and open palm address Him beyond the right edge, keeping Him unseen. The lakeside, boat, village, clothing details and number of visible men are artistic staging; the distant gathering evokes the people referred to as them. The image does not supply His answer.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four robed men sit on rocks beneath an olive tree beside a blue lake, looking attentively to the left. One holds an open palm. A smaller group sits beneath distant trees, with a shoreline village and pale hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The lakeside setting and two groups are imaginative. Nearby listeners attending to Jesus outside the frame suggest the knowledge granted 'to you'; the distant group recalls 'to them it has not been granted.' Distance and natural light are visual devices, not causes of understanding or claims about anyone's final salvation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of two clay bowls on a sunlit stone ledge. A linen-sleeved hand pours golden grain into an overflowing bowl; another holds a scoop with a few kernels above an almost empty bowl. An earthenware jar, olive branches and distant hills complete the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The abundant bowl receiving more grain illustrates the promise of increase. The nearly bare bowl and the few kernels held above it serve as an imaginative reminder of the warning that even what one has will be taken away. These ordinary objects form an analogy, not a narrated event or a portrayal of God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of robed villagers seated beneath an olive tree beside a blue lake. An older bearded man and a veiled woman look left with furrowed brows; behind them, two men turn toward one another, one raising an open palm. Golden grasses, distant hills and pale buildings surround the gathering.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined audience suggests outward seeing and hearing without understanding through open eyes, puzzled faces and a questioning gesture. Jesus remains outside the frame. The lakeside setting and arrangement of listeners are imaginative, not details stated in this verse; the image does not portray physical blindness or deafness.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed adults sit beneath an olive tree in a sunlit stone courtyard, looking left with puzzled expressions. The woman holds a palm open. A blank unrolled scroll rests on a foreground ledge, with a clay jar and small flowers nearby; hills and stone houses lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard groups listeners who look toward an off-frame speaker yet appear perplexed, suggesting the verse's contrast between hearing or looking and understanding or perceiving. The blank scroll alludes to Isaiah's prophecy without reproducing its words. The setting and gestures are illustrative, not details supplied by the verse; Jesus is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed adults sit beneath an olive tree beside a stone wall. A bearded man closes his eyes and folds his arms; a woman closes her eyes with a hand over her ear; a third figure turns away. A sunlit path curves past wildflowers toward olive groves, blue hills and distant houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined hillside grouping gives visible form to closed eyes, reluctant hearing and a dulled heart through the adults' inward, resistant gestures. The open path and warm natural light suggest the possibility of returning and restoration. These are compositional metaphors, not a narrated gathering or an actual cure. Jesus remains outside the frame.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in ochre, sage, and russet robes sit on pale rocks beneath an olive tree, smiling attentively toward the upper left. A blue lake, distant village and hills, grasses, and small wildflowers surround them in a warm, textured painted scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined lakeside gathering gives visible form to the blessing of seeing and hearing: open eyes, a visible ear, and attentive faces turn toward the unseen teacher. Jesus remains beyond the frame. The verse does not specify these men, their seating, or this landscape; the image illustrates receptive attention rather than a healing.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four robed men sit beneath an olive tree, looking attentively toward the upper left. Three tied parchment scrolls rest on a stone in front of them; blue water, a village and distant hills fill the warm watercolor background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The listeners imagine the disciples' privilege of seeing and hearing Jesus, who remains outside the frame. The aged scrolls recall the prophets and righteous people who longed for what these disciples receive. This arrangement is a visual meditation, not an event or collection of scrolls stated in the verse; it does not place earlier prophets among the disciples.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three adults in loose earth-toned robes sit beneath an olive tree, smiling attentively toward the upper left. An open woven pouch spills golden grain onto a foreground stone. Furrowed fields, olive trees, a distant village and hills fill the sunlit background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The attentive listeners imaginatively express the command to hear. The seed pouch and worked field recall the sower whose parable they are invited to hear. Jesus remains outside the frame. The verse does not specify these people, objects or this setting; the image supplies a contemplative scene rather than a documented arrangement.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three brown birds on a sunlit earthen path beside plowed soil: one lifts off carrying a golden grain, one bends to pick up another, and one stands nearby. Scattered seeds, olive trees, small flowers, distant hills and pale village buildings fill the warm watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative field scene uses birds taking exposed grains to illustrate the snatching-away through the sower's agricultural imagery. The hard path represents the hearer who does not understand. The verse identifies the evil one as the one who takes what was sown in the heart; the birds are an indirect illustration, not his literal appearance. The landscape is not a documented event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling man in a cream tunic and terracotta mantle sits among pale rocks, one hand against his chest. Fresh green shoots rise from small pockets of soil in front of him. Olive trees, hills and a distant village stand beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The anonymous listener and fresh shoots form an imaginative pairing: his joyful attention evokes immediately receiving the word, while the soil among stones recalls the rocky ground. This is an illustration of the teaching, not a recorded encounter. Jesus remains outside the picture, and the later outcome is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a drooping young plant with green and ochre leaves and exposed roots in a thin patch of dry soil on pale limestone. Sunlit hills, a blue lake, distant buildings and dark slender trees recede behind it.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined wilted plant and roots confined to shallow soil picture a hearer without an enduring inward root. Dry heat is a visual analogy for tribulation or persecution because of the word. This is an illustration of the teaching, not a recorded event; the verse describes a person falling away, not a botanical observation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Slender green grain shoots without seed heads stand crowded by arching thorny brambles. A worn leather purse and a few golden coins rest on the stony soil beside them. Warm watercolor hills, terraced fields and olive trees recede into the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative field scene follows the verse's seed-and-thorns comparison. The crowded, unfruitful shoots evoke the hearer whose reception of the word is stifled by worldly cares and deceptive riches. The purse is an added visual reference to riches, not an object stated to be present in the parable or a claim about a historical event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three tied wheat sheaves of increasing fullness stand on dark soil scattered with grains and seedlings. Golden wheat fills the field behind them, with olive trees, a distant village and lavender hills beneath a sunny blue sky. Small white and purple flowers grow among foreground stones.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative harvest composition pictures the verse's good soil and fruitfulness. The three bundles of differing fullness suggest the hundredfold, sixtyfold and thirtyfold yields without claiming exact grain counts. Hearing and understanding the word are the spiritual relationship explained by the verse; the field is an illustration, not a recorded event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A linen-sleeved hand scatters golden grain onto reddish furrows beside an open woven seed pouch. A low stone wall, olive trees, a distant village and hills sit beneath a softly lit blue-and-peach sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative close view shows the man sowing good seed in his own field, the comparison Jesus uses for the kingdom of heaven. The sleeve, seed pouch, stone wall and rural landscape are illustrative setting details, not details specified by this verse. Jesus remains outside the image, and no later event in the parable is shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Moonlit watercolor of a cloaked man walking along a field path, scattering seeds from an open hand among young wheat. Two men sleep beneath a reed shelter behind him. Stone walls, an olive tree, distant houses and purple hills surround the field.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The cloaked sower represents the owner's enemy. His departing stride and falling seeds picture the secret sowing of weeds among wheat while others sleep. Moonlight, the shelter, village and clothing are imaginative setting details, not details specified by the verse. The scene illustrates the parable without depicting Jesus or God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of full golden-green grain heads and slender branching grass seed heads growing together in warm earth, with curling leaves, a broad field, ochre hills and a pale blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative close view uses grain-bearing wheat and contrasting wild grasses to picture the weeds becoming evident as the crop grows. The particular plant shapes, light and hills are illustrative choices, not details specified by the verse. Nothing is harvested or uprooted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in long earth-colored robes stand beside a stone farmhouse. The nearer man looks off-frame and extends an open hand toward golden wheat intermingled with slender green and brown weed spikes. Olive trees, a stone wall and distant hills fill the warm watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene places two of the parable's servants beside the mixed crop as they question the householder, who remains outside the frame. Their concerned expressions and the rooted wheat and weeds convey the contrast between good seed and the unexpected growth. The number of servants, their appearance and the farmhouse setting are artistic choices; the image does not supply the answer to their question.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of two robed men beside golden wheat and dark seed-headed weeds. One crouches and points at a plant; the other stands with an open palm. Both look beyond the picture. A stone wall, olive trees and pale hills recede behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The mixed wheat and dark weeds visualize the trouble attributed to an enemy. The servants' pointing and open palm suggest their request to gather the weeds; nothing has been uprooted. The field, clothing and gestures are imaginative details of the parable. The householder remains outside the frame, and neither Jesus nor God is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of green-gold wheat and fine-stemmed weeds growing together above intertwined roots in an exposed earthen bank. A linen-sleeved hand pauses beside a stem while another raises an open palm. Sunlit fields, hills and distant pale buildings fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined field-edge close-up illustrates the warning about uprooting wheat while gathering weeds. Intertwined roots make the danger visible, while the paused reaching hand and open stopping gesture express restraint. The anonymous workers are illustrative details, not portraits of Jesus or God; the verse does not describe this particular view.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a kneeling laborer tying slender weeds beside ripe wheat. Bound weeds lie nearby, and a small fire burns a separate pile on bare earth. Another worker carries golden wheat toward an open stone storehouse, with sheaves at its doorway and hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative harvest scene illustrates the future work commanded in the parable: weeds that grew among the wheat are separated and bound for burning, while the good wheat is carried into storage. It shows the agricultural picture rather than Jesus speaking or a literal depiction of divine judgment. The workers, building and landscape are imagined details. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A weathered hand emerging from a cream woven sleeve holds a small golden seed above a hollow in reddish tilled soil. Furrows, grasses, stones, olive trees, distant hills and a small village recede beneath a pale blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined close view illustrates the man sowing the mustard seed within Jesus' parable. The hand belongs to an ordinary farmer, not a portrayal of Jesus or God. The clothing and countryside are artistic setting details; the kingdom of heaven is conveyed through the verse's comparison. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a yellow-flowering tree-like plant above low garden herbs, with five brown songbirds in its branches, one with wings raised. A tiny round seed and larger pale grains rest on a foreground stone; a low stone wall and distant hills lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The small seed beside larger grains and the mature branching plant share one imaginative garden scene to express the verse's contrast between a small beginning and abundant growth. The birds lodging in its branches follow the verse directly. The seed display, flowers and garden details are illustrative choices, not a recorded event or a botanical identification supplied by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman in an olive dress and cream head covering folds pale dough over a tan starter in a broad wooden trough. Three flour-dusted clay vessels stand beside it in a sunlit stone courtyard beneath a leafy trellis.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household scene pictures the bread-making comparison in Jesus' parable, with the small starter being hidden within a large batch. The three vessels recall the three measures of flour; their form and the courtyard are artistic choices. A single moment cannot show the elapsed fermentation: the verse says the leaven eventually worked through the whole.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor crowd in earth-toned robes sits beneath leafy trees beside a blue lake. An older gray-bearded man, a woman in a cream head covering, a younger bearded man and a child gaze toward the upper right. Flowers and limestone rocks fill the foreground; hills and pale buildings line the far shore.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The listeners' shared attention imaginatively evokes the crowds hearing Jesus speak in parables. Jesus remains outside the picture. Their individual appearances, the lakeside setting and their expressions are artistic choices, not details specified by this verse. The image does not identify a particular parable or assert that everyone understood.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a blank unfurled parchment on weathered stones beneath an olive tree. A terracotta bowl holds seeds beside scattered grains and green seedlings with exposed roots. Wildflowers edge the terrace, with a blue lake and hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The unfurled scroll evokes the prophet's words reaching fulfillment; seeds and newly visible roots imaginatively suggest ordinary images disclosing hidden things. These objects and the garden are a visual meditation, not an event or setting specified by the verse. Jesus is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five robed men gather inside a sunlit stone house, looking toward the right. The central man raises an open hand. Wheat ears and green weed stems rest on a low wooden table, while several people walk away outside the open doorway.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The indoor group imagines the disciples approaching Jesus with their question; He remains outside the image. Departing figures recall the crowds left behind. Wheat and weed stems are an imaginative cue to the parable, not objects the verse says were present. The house, faces and arrangement are illustrative.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A linen-lined woven basket filled with golden grain rests beside curved, freshly tilled furrows dotted with seeds. An olive tree shades the foreground; stone terraces, olive groves, hillside houses and blue hills recede beneath a softly clouded sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The basket of good grain and seeded furrows imaginatively evoke the sowing in Jesus' answer. The verse identifies the sower as the Son of Man, who remains out of view. This composition meditates on His explanation rather than claiming that He performed a farming action while speaking.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Golden wheat and slender green weeds grow together in a sunlit field. A pale stone village, blue-violet hills, and soft clouds lie beyond. Fine drawn contours and textured watercolor washes fill the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative field illustrates the parable rather than a recorded event. Its broad landscape suggests the world; the fruitful wheat recalls the good seed, identified as sons of the kingdom, while the intermingled weeds recall the sons of the evil one. The plants visualize the distinct identities named in the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two winged angels in cream robes gather golden wheat at sunset. The nearer angel holds a curved sickle; tied sheaves and dark weed stalks fill the foreground beneath a peach and lavender sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative harvest scene focuses on the verse's identification of the reapers as angels. The sunset suggests completion of the age, while dark weeds among the wheat recall the enemy's sowing. Wings, robes and setting are artistic choices, not details supplied by the verse. The devil is named in the explanation but is not pictured; neither God nor Jesus is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Uprooted weeds with tangled roots and dark seed heads burn in orange flames on bare earth. Embers and ash lie beneath, with another gathered clump in the foreground, harvested stubble, olive trees, distant hills and a small village under a warm evening sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined harvest setting pictures the verse's comparison: gathered weeds are consumed by fire. The exposed roots, gathered clump and ash make that action visible. The late-day light is an artistic setting, not a claim about when the end of the age occurs; the scene does not depict the final judgment itself.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three winged angels in ivory robes work beside a flowering garden wall. One gathers thorny branches and rope in the foreground while two guide four robed adults outward through a stone opening toward sunlit hills. Olive branches arch overhead.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative garden represents His kingdom. Angels guiding adults outward visualize the gathering of those practicing lawlessness. The thorns and ropes symbolize causes of sin; these objects and the garden setting are artistic choices, not details named in the verse. Christ remains unseen. The scene illustrates the solemn removal without adding the punishment described elsewhere.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed men huddle inside the arched mouth of a stone furnace amid orange flames. Two cover their faces, while the third raises his face with an anguished expression. Dark rocks and smoky shadows surround the glowing masonry.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative furnace scene visualizes the verse's fire and anguish through clothed figures and grieving gestures. The masonry and arrangement are illustrative details, not details supplied by the Greek. The casting act is not shown; the image depicts its fearful aftermath without graphic injuries.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six modestly robed men and women glow with golden light on a flowered hillside beneath a bright sun. A foreground listener in a blue mantle holds a hand beside an ear. A leafy tree, winding stone path and distant hills frame the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The flowered hillside is an imaginative setting, not a location supplied by the verse. Light around the six people visualizes the promise that the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom; the foreground listener's hand beside the ear echoes the command to hear. No figure represents God or Jesus.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling man in an ochre headcloth and earth-colored robes kneels beside a partly buried terracotta jar filled with coins, holding a coarse cloth over its opening. Green plants, small flowers, a stone wall, olive trees, distant hills and a village surround the sunlit field.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined jar, clothing and landscape give visual form to the parable; the verse does not specify these details. His smile and the cloth over the treasure suggest the joy of finding it and hiding it again. The subsequent sale of everything and purchase of the field are explained by the verse rather than shown in this single moment.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded merchant in a cream tunic, indigo mantle and wrapped headcloth examines a pearl beneath an ochre awning. Several pale pearls lie in a linen-lined wooden tray on the counter. Earthen vessels and a sunlit stone arch frame the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined market scene gives visible form to the comparison: a merchant carefully examines fine pearls. His attentive search reflects the action named in the verse. The setting and appearance are artistic choices; the purchase described in the following verse is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling, bearded man in cream and olive robes receives a single pearl from an older seller across a wooden counter. An open leather purse, silver-colored coins and an indigo cloth lie below their hands. Warm stone arches, pink flowers and a sunlit market fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined market purchase brings the verse's final action into view. The single pearl focuses its great value; the emptied purse and paid coins suggest the proceeds of selling all he had. The market, clothing and gestures are artistic details rather than details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A broad, cork-floated net encloses fish of many shapes and sizes in clear blue-green water. Two robed fishermen tend ropes from a wooden boat near a rocky shore, with trees, a distant village and low hills beneath a warm sunset sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The fishermen, boat, sunset and shoreline are imagined setting details, not details specified by this verse. The unusually clear water makes the varied catch visible. The net gathering many kinds of fish illustrates Jesus' comparison with the kingdom of heaven; the later sorting is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two seated fishermen sort a large catch on a sunlit lakeshore. One places a silver fish into a woven basket; the other casts a fish toward several lying apart on the sand. A laden net fills the foreground, with a wooden boat, blue water, hills and distant buildings behind.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative lakeshore reconstruction pictures the parable's literal sorting: fish gathered into baskets and rejected fish cast aside. The fishermen, boat, landscape, clothing and precise appearance of the catch are illustrative choices, not details specified by the verse. Jesus is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A warm watercolor hillside beneath an amber sky. One white-robed, winged angel extends a hand beside a quiet gathering on the left; another accompanies three downcast adults along a path on the right. Open ground separates the groups, with wildflowers, rocks and blue-violet hills around them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The separating groups illustrate the verse's statement that angels will remove the wicked from among the righteous at the end of the age. The hillside, gestures, clothing and feathered wings are imaginative choices, not details specified by the verse. The scene shows solemn separation; the following verse's punishment is outside this image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of three robed men behind a low stone ledge inside a blazing arched furnace. One looks upward in anguish, one covers his face, and one bows over clasped hands. Orange fire lights rough stone against a smoky, barren landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined stone furnace gives visual form to the verse's furnace of fire; the three grieving adults suggest weeping and gnashing of teeth. Their number, clothing and setting are artistic choices, not details stated in the verse. The scene withholds the act of casting and graphic injury while retaining the warning of judgment.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six bearded men in cream tunics and red, green, blue and striped mantles sit closely on woven mats in a sunlit stone room. They look toward the upper left; the central man raises an open hand near his chest. A clay jug stands at lower left, with olive branches visible through the doorway.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The six disciples' attentive faces and the central man's open hand imaginatively picture the group's spoken "Yes." Jesus remains beyond the frame. The room, clothing colors, number shown and gestures are artistic choices; the verse records the question about understanding all these things and their affirmative answer, without describing those visual details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded householder in cream robes and an ochre mantle lifts a pale tied scroll beside an older brown roll on a wooden table. An open chest holds more scrolls and folded cloth. A clay lamp burns nearby, with olive branches visible through the sunlit window.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household illustrates Jesus' comparison, rather than an event the verse records. Fresh and worn scrolls stand for the new and old treasures a scribe discipled for the kingdom brings forth. The verse names treasures, not scrolls; these objects connect the householder's store with the scribe's learning. Jesus remains outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An empty sunlit stone courtyard beneath a spreading olive tree. Low stone seats stand in the shade, and footprints cross the dust through an open stone gateway onto a winding path toward golden fields, distant buildings, and blue hills. Small white and purple flowers grow in the foreground.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The empty gathering place and footprints leading away imaginatively connect the completion of Jesus' parables with His departure. The courtyard, olive tree, gateway, footprints, and warm afternoon light are artistic staging; the verse does not specify them. Jesus remains outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six listeners in earth-colored robes sit on stone benches in a warmly lit synagogue. An older gray-bearded man extends an open hand, two men turn toward one another, and others look upward to the left with wondering expressions. A doorway opens onto sunlit village houses and hills; a rolled parchment rests nearby.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative synagogue interior centers the townspeople's astonishment and questioning as Jesus teaches in His home region. Their glances toward an unseen speaker keep Jesus outside the frame. The faces, gestures and room are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse. Their wonder relates to both His wisdom and the miraculous powers they mention; no miracle is shown occurring here.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed neighbors converse beside a sunlit carpenter's bench holding a small wooden stool, chisels, a mallet, an axe and curled shavings. An older man extends his palm while the other man and a head-covered woman listen thoughtfully. A stone doorway, clay jar, olive branches and village lane surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative workshop setting connects the speakers' questions to the carpenter and familiar household named in the verse. The three figures are anonymous questioning neighbors, not Mary or the four named brothers. The scene does not claim that this conversation occurred at a workshop or that the family gathered there. Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed men gesture with open hands in a sunlit stone village lane. Behind them, four women in long dresses and head coverings gather at a doorway; one holds a clay jar. Olive branches, terracotta vessels, pale houses and green hills fill the warm, textured watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined village conversation places questioning neighbors before a group of women, evoking the speakers' appeal to Jesus' sisters being among them. The women's number, appearances, courtyard and gestures are artistic choices, not details supplied by the verse. No woman is identified as a particular sister, and Jesus remains outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five adults in earth-toned robes gather beside a sunlit stone house. A standing man folds his arms, a seated man looks back with a furrowed brow, and a woman turns toward the doorway. Olive branches, clay jars, distant village houses, and hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined village doorway and guarded, turned-away neighbors evoke the hometown and household that withhold honor. These figures are not identified relatives or a reconstruction of a specific encounter. Jesus remains outside the frame; the image reflects the rejection stated in the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed villagers stand beside a wooden doorway beneath an olive tree. A bearded man folds his arms, an older man turns aside, and a shawled woman looks down. Clay jars and flowers border a sunlit stone lane leading toward village houses and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The villagers' guarded expressions and the quiet lane imaginatively suggest the unbelief named in the verse. These particular people, gestures and setting are artistic choices, not details supplied by the verse. No miracle is pictured, and Jesus remains out of view; the stillness does not claim that He performed no mighty works or lacked power.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a bearded captive seated on a stone bench, wearing a cream tunic and rough brown cloak. Iron cuffs and a short chain bind his wrists. A clay jug stands beside him, sunlight enters through a high barred window, and a guard is visible beyond the closed barred door.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John's chained wrists and barred cell illustrate the verse's binding and imprisonment. The stone room, clothing, guard, jug, and sunlight are imaginative setting details, not details supplied by the verse. Herod and Herodias are left outside the scene; the light suggests no release or miraculous event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A troubled ruler in a crimson mantle and gold circlet sits on a carved chair, extending an open hand toward two attentive men in olive and cream robes. Warm watercolor washes show a stone palace arch, courtyard greenery, pottery and fruit.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined palace conversation depicts Herod voicing his claim to attentive servants. His tense expression suggests unease; the setting, clothing and gestures are illustrative choices. Jesus and John remain unseen, so the image does not present Herod's claim of John's resurrection as an event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a rough brown robe standing with one palm raised toward a seated man wearing cream and crimson robes and a gold laurel wreath. Stone arches frame distant hills and buildings; olive foliage and clay vessels stand in the sunlit courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John's raised palm imagines the firmness of his repeated rebuke that it was not lawful for the man to have her. The seated ruler's troubled expression suggests resistance to correction. The courtyard, clothing, wreath and gestures are imaginative details, not descriptions supplied by this verse. The woman remains outside the picture, addressing the unlawful relationship indirectly.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four robed men gather on sunlit stone steps beneath olive branches. One gestures while holding a rolled scroll; another holds a wooden lyre, and a frame drum rests at their feet. Blue hills and pale stone houses recede behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative gathering of singers illustrates the heading's address to the music director and association with the sons of Korah. The courtyard, instruments and individual men are artistic choices, not a documented event. Maskil remains a traditional title with an uncertain precise sense.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in cream and rust robes kneels beside a low stone wall with open hands raised toward the sky. Three men gather near a sunlit town gate; one points toward him. Olive branches, flowers and golden hills frame the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The kneeling petitioner and distant men at the gate imaginatively express an appeal for God's judgment amid deceit and injustice. The verse gives no town-gate scene or physical description; these details are illustrative. God remains unseen, and the sunlight conveys hope rather than a pictured divine appearance.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A wooden lyre, round frame drum and tied parchment roll rest on cream linen over a sunlit stone bench. Olive branches hang above them, with olive trees and blue-violet hills beyond a low wall. Small wildflowers grow between the foreground stones.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The instruments and tied scroll form an imaginative preparation for sacred song, relating to the heading's music director and sons of Korah. The verse does not specify these instruments or this courtyard. The still life evokes its musical setting without claiming a narrated event or a historical reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A wooden lyre leans against a sunlit stone bench beside white lilies in a clay jug, a blank parchment scroll and folded linen. Olive branches frame a stone arch, distant houses and blue hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The lyre and quiet courtyard imagine preparation for the love song named in the superscription. The lilies echo its musical heading without claiming that the heading describes literal flowers or a known performance setting. The blank parchment suggests a song awaiting expression; this still-life does not depict a narrated event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five robed men gather in a golden stone courtyard. A standing leader raises a hand toward four singers, one seated with a wooden lyre. Olive branches and pink flowers frame an archway overlooking sunlit hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard rehearsal connects the leader and singers with the heading and its association with the sons of Korah. The lyre and setting are illustrative choices, not details stated by this verse. The image makes no claim about the precise meaning of Alamoth.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four men in cream, olive and terracotta robes make music in a sunlit stone courtyard. A seated gray-bearded man gestures with an open hand between two seated lyre players, while a standing singer holds a hand to his chest. Olive branches arch overhead, with pale hills and buildings beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined musical fellowship evokes the heading naming the music director and the sons of Korah. The lyres and shared singing suggest a psalm prepared for worship. The courtyard, clothing, instruments and individual figures are artistic choices, not an event or specific details narrated by this heading.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two wooden lyres and a low stringed psaltery rest by a stone bench with a striped linen cloth. Warm sunlight fills the courtyard; a clay jar and overhanging leaves sit at left, while a stone arch opens toward cypress trees and distant hills beneath a pink-blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The instruments and quiet courtyard imaginatively evoke preparation for the psalm's musical performance, recalling its association with the director and the sons of Korah. The heading names no instruments or location; these details are illustrative, not a reconstruction of a recorded scene.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in cream robes and earth-colored mantles sing in a sunlit stone courtyard. The seated man plays a wooden lyre while two companions stand beside him. Olive branches shade the paving; a clay jar rests near the tree.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The singers and lyre imaginatively evoke the song and psalm associated with the sons of Korah. The courtyard, clothing and gathering are illustrative choices; the heading does not specify these people, instruments or a setting.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed figures, including a child holding an adult's hand, stand beside an olive tree overlooking golden fields, stone villages, a winding stream, mountains and the sea. A low sun glows at the left while rose clouds color the right.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined listeners and continuous landscape suggest the whole earth attending God's call. Dawn at the left and evening colors at the right poetically join rising and setting; the verse does not describe these people, this location or a simultaneous sky. God remains unseen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A golden wooden lyre leans against a limestone bench draped with cream cloth. A tied parchment roll rests beside it, with a clay jar, an olive tree, sunlit paving and distant hills completing the watercolor courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The lyre evokes the heading's address to the choirmaster and association with David. The tied roll and quiet courtyard offer an imaginative setting for attentive music and reflection.
