scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a cream robe and russet mantle kneeling on a sunlit stone terrace, both hands raised toward the sky. An olive tree and wildflowers frame rolling groves and distant hills beneath warm morning clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The anonymous worshipper imaginatively expresses the resolve to exalt God and bless His name. God, addressed as King, remains unseen; neither the man nor the sunrise represents Him. The verse specifies no location, clothing or gesture. This quiet setting is an artistic meditation, not a recorded episode, and one moment of praise can only suggest the promise to continue forever.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream tunic and rust-brown mantle kneels beside an olive tree, looking upward with both hands open in prayer. Warm sunrise lights rocky ground, small flowers, distant blue hills and a stone village in a textured watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined worshipper and his open hands express the verse's earnest prayer and supplications. His hopeful upward gaze suggests reliance on the LORD's faithfulness and righteousness. The hillside and sunrise are artistic setting choices, not details stated in the verse or proof of an answer already given. God remains unseen; the figure is not an asserted likeness of David.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a cream tunic and russet cloak seated on a rocky ledge, looking upward while holding a wooden bow and touching its string. A round shield and quiver stand beside him. Olive trees, flowers, distant hills and a village lie beneath a low golden sun.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative psalmist-warrior represents the first-person speaker, not a documented event or historical likeness of David. His bow, shield and attentive fingers retain the verse's preparation for battle; his lifted face suggests grateful praise. The solid rock evokes the LORD's dependable strength without portraying God. The hillside and village are imagined surroundings. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor clouds with golden and peach-lit edges and lavender shadows surround a broad blue sky. Wispy clouds cross the upper sky, while a warm glow spreads along a distant horizon above layered cloud banks.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined expanse of high clouds evokes the heavens and heights from which the verse summons praise to the LORD. Dawn light and the upward sweep express wonder and delight; they do not portray God or document a particular event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream tunic and blue-gray mantle looks upward beneath an olive tree, one hand over his chest and the other raised. A stony path and wildflowers overlook terraced olive groves, a distant stone village and lavender hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The unnamed worshipper's hand over his heart and uplifted palm imaginatively express the call for one's own soul to praise the LORD. The hillside, clothing and morning setting are artistic choices; the verse names no person, place or event. God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A gray-bearded man plays a wooden lyre among four other singers, including a child, in a sunlit stone courtyard. One man lifts a hand, and the others sing with open hands or a hand over the heart. Olive branches, flowers, distant buildings and hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering gives visible form to the call to sing praise: shared song and lyre accompaniment express praise as good, pleasant and fitting. The people, instrument and courtyard are illustrative choices, not a named event or details specified by the verse. God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six robed worshippers raise their hands or gaze upward in a sunlit stone courtyard. A small sanctuary stands beyond them beneath a wide blue sky filled with luminous clouds; olive branches and flowers frame the paving.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The anonymous gathering imagines the call to praise God in His sanctuary, while the open sky evokes the firmament of His might. The people, courtyard and sanctuary design are illustrative choices, not an event or an exact historical reconstruction supplied by the verse. God is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor of children, adults and elders singing with lifted faces and open hands in a sunlit stone courtyard, framed by olive branches, flowers and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The anonymous singers imagine the faithful assembly called to praise the LORD with a new song. The verse names no particular people, place or historical occasion; the courtyard, clothing and gestures are imaginative choices. Their shared singing illustrates communal praise without depicting God or claiming to show the words or newness of the song.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in an ivory tunic and brown mantle and a woman in a terracotta dress and cream head covering holding hands beside an open wooden door. A clay jar, reed mat, sunlit earthen walls and a date palm surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Their joined hands suggest the marriage of a man from Levi's family and a woman of the same lineage. The verse does not specify their appearance, clothing, home or a wedding rite; this quiet household setting is an imaginative aid, not a reconstruction. Levi is not pictured as a separate person.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an elderly gray-bearded man in a cream robe, head cloth and rust-brown mantle among sunlit desert rocks. He looks upward with a troubled expression, one hand against his chest and the other extended palm-up. An empty rocky path leads toward violet hills beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses's questioning hand and troubled face visualize his fear of not being believed. His appearance, clothing and the rocky landscape are imaginative choices. The verse records his reply, not an encounter with rejecting listeners, so he stands alone. God is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A gray-bearded shepherd in a cream robe, brown mantle and pale headcloth walks with sheep and goats along a rocky desert path. He holds a curved wooden staff and looks toward a high, sunlit mountain beneath a blue sky with soft clouds. Warm watercolor colors show stones, sparse shrubs and textured wool.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures Moses leading Jethro's flock to Horeb on the far side of the wilderness. The mountain, path, staff, clothing and face are illustrative choices, not a historical reconstruction. Jethro is named as the owner but is not pictured. The scene stays with this verse's shepherding journey, before the burning bush described next; God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of two elderly bearded men standing before an Egyptian ruler seated on a blue-and-gold throne. The man in a rust mantle extends an open hand; his companion wears olive. Papyrus columns frame sunlit desert hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses and Aaron addressing Pharaoh visualizes the verse's spoken demand that Israel be released to feast to the LORD in the wilderness. Their faces, garments, and palace are imaginative conventions, not historical likenesses or certain archaeology. The desert view recalls the requested destination; the feast is not shown as already happening. God remains unseen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A gray-bearded man in a cream robe and brown woven mantle kneels among sunlit rocks, one hand over his chest and his gaze lifted. An empty sandy road curves toward a closed mudbrick gateway, with palms, reeds and distant hills under a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' listening posture and the Egyptian setting are imaginative; the verse does not locate this speech. The closed gateway suggests Pharaoh's power, while the empty sunlit road anticipates the promised release without showing it already fulfilled. God remains unseen, and the repeated mighty hand is understood as power rather than pictured as a hand in the sky.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of two elderly bearded men in cream robes and rust and olive mantles in a sunlit courtyard. The man at left offers an open hand; the other rests one hand on his chest and extends the other toward a columned Egyptian gateway. Palms rise beyond ochre walls.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The brothers' attentive exchange imagines Moses bearing God's delegated authority and Aaron preparing to be his prophet and spokesman. The courtyard and gestures are artistic choices; this verse does not name a location or describe an audience with Pharaoh. God remains unseen, and Moses is portrayed as human. Their appearances and the architecture are imaginative conventions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two gray-bearded men in long cream robes stand beside a reed-lined river. The nearer man, wearing a rust-colored mantle, extends a wooden staff over the water while the man behind gestures with an open hand. Frogs gather on the sandy bank and swim among the reeds; palms and flat-roofed buildings stand across the water.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The scene imagines Moses relaying the LORD's command and Aaron extending his staff over Egypt's waters. Emerging frogs visualize the sign being commanded; this verse gives the instruction rather than narrating its completed fulfillment. Clothing, faces, and riverbank buildings are artistic conventions. God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, gray-bearded Moses in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle stands with one hand on his chest and the other on a wooden staff. Warm ochre courtyard walls surround him; an open gateway reveals an empty sandy road, distant houses, palms and hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses listens solemnly beside an imagined Egyptian gateway. The empty road anticipates God's promise that Pharaoh will drive the people out after one more plague; it does not show the departure as already happening. The verse names neither this courtyard nor the time of day. God and the coming plague remain unseen; the likeness, clothing and architecture are artistic conventions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle approaches closed wooden palace doors. His open hand is raised near his chest. Tall sandstone columns with teal and ochre details, palm trees and a blue sky surround the sunlit approach.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' approach is an imaginative response to the command to go to Pharaoh, not an arrival narrated in this verse. The shut palace doors suggest the hardened resistance of Pharaoh and his servants; they are a visual metaphor, not literal hearts. The LORD's stated purpose is to set His signs among them. God, Pharaoh, his servants and the signs remain out of view; the architecture and clothing are imaginative.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A gray-bearded Moses in a cream robe and russet mantle extends an open hand toward Pharaoh, who sits in ivory robes and a blue-and-gold headcloth on an ornate throne. Warm sandstone columns, potted palms, a woven mat, and a sunlit courtyard surround them in a textured watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The scene imaginatively visualizes the audience Moses is commanded to seek, with his open hand suggesting the demand to release the Hebrews for service to the Lord. The verse gives the command, rather than narrating this meeting or Pharaoh granting release. God remains unseen; faces, clothing, and palace details are artistic conventions. No later plague is pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two elderly bearded men in long earth-toned robes stand listening with uplifted faces in a sunlit mud-brick courtyard. One wears a rust-colored mantle; the other has a cream shawl. A clay jar rests by the wall, with water, reeds, palms and low houses beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses and Aaron are imagined listening reverently to the LORD in Egypt; God remains unseen. Their faces, everyday clothing, courtyard, riverside landscape and daylight are artistic choices, not details specified by this verse. Their shared attention expresses receiving His words without picturing the speaker or adding the later instructions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in a cream robe, rust-colored mantle and cloth head covering stands among sunlit desert rocks. He looks upward, one hand on his chest and the other holding a wooden staff. Sparse plants and layered mountains stretch beneath a blue, cloud-dappled sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' upward gaze and quiet posture imagine his attention as the LORD speaks. The wilderness, clothing and staff are illustrative choices; this verse does not specify them or yet state the message. God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, gray-bearded man in a cream robe, head covering and russet mantle stands among desert rocks and small flowering shrubs. He holds a wooden staff, rests one hand on his chest and looks upward beneath a blue sky, with ochre hills behind him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses listening alone offers an imaginative visual relationship to the LORD speaking to him. The desert, clothing and attentive pose are artistic choices; this verse does not specify them. God remains unseen, and no details of the following command are pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a rocky desert camp, a worried woman holds an empty bowl beside a child. A seated man in a blue mantle examines a waterskin. Tents and arriving families stretch into the dry valley, with baskets, bundles, and rolled blankets in the foreground.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined family, empty bowl, and waterskin bring the lack of drinking water close to view, while arriving travelers and tents suggest the whole congregation camping at Rephidim. Their faces, clothing, possessions, and the valley's appearance are illustrative choices, not details specified by the verse. The LORD's command is not given a visible form, and the scene does not anticipate the later water-from-the-rock event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of families walking through a sunlit rocky desert. A woman in a terracotta robe holds a child's hand beside a man carrying a rolled blanket and an older man with a staff. Travelers with baskets, bundles and pack animals form a long procession across the valley beneath blue mountains.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The winding procession visualizes the whole congregation's journey from Elim into the wilderness of Sin. The families, garments, carried bundles and rocky landscape are imaginative details, not identified portraits or a reconstruction of the route. The verse's fifteenth day of the second month is retained in the explanation rather than encoded in the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly white-bearded man in cream and brown robes holds a wooden staff and raises one hand while singing. Men, women, and children sing around him on a rocky shore beside a blue, foaming sea, with sunlit hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined shore gathering focuses on Moses and Israel singing to the LORD after His glorious triumph. The sea recalls the song's declaration that He hurled horse and rider into it; that destruction is left outside the pictured moment. Faces, clothing, gestures, and landscape are artistic conventions, not historical likenesses or archaeological claims.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Seven people in cream, blue and rust robes sit among desert rocks and small flowers, facing a sunlit ochre mountain whose upper slopes are veiled in lavender-gray clouds. Fine contours and warm watercolor washes show textured paper.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The seated listeners and mountain under clouds imaginatively evoke reverent attention as God begins to speak. Exodus 20:1 itself names God as speaker and introduces His words; it does not describe these people, poses, colors or landscape details. God is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in cream and ochre robes listens with a hand on his chest as a younger man in muted teal gestures toward him. They sit on a woven rug beside a dark desert tent, with a clay jug and cup, an overhanging tree, and sunlit rocky mountains.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Jethro's hearing is pictured through an imagined conversation with an unnamed traveler. The verse does not identify how the news reached him or describe his face, clothing, or surroundings. The tent and Midian landscape provide an imaginative setting; Moses and the events reported remain outside the picture. His attentive expression suggests wonder at the LORD's deliverance without depicting God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man, woman and child in earth-toned robes overlook a rocky desert valley with staffs, rolled bedding and water jars. A long line of travelers and a laden donkey winds toward rose-colored mountains beneath a blue, cloud-dappled sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The family and procession imagine Israel arriving in Sinai's wilderness. Their faces, clothing, travel gear, donkey and the particular mountain shapes are artistic choices; the verse supplies the people, arrival, place and third-month timing. The landscape is an imaginative setting rather than a historically verified view of Sinai.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A solemn man holds an oil lamp beside a breached mudbrick house. A cloaked, motionless figure lies among fallen bricks, with sandaled feet visible. A digging tool and tied sack rest nearby beneath a blue evening sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined aftermath relates the breached wall and digging tool to breaking in, and the covered, motionless figure to the thief's death. The householder, lamp, dim light and courtyard are artistic staging. The legal ruling of no bloodguilt remains in the explanation; the picture illustrates the case without showing the fatal blow.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man in a cream robe and blue mantle raises an open palm toward a rust-cloaked man whispering and extending his hand. Behind them, a standing man addresses two elders beneath an awning in a sunlit desert camp.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined camp hearing illustrates a command, not a recorded event. The blue-cloaked man refusing the whispering man's offered hand represents rejecting false reports and complicity in unjust testimony. The anonymous people, clothing and setting are artistic conventions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an elderly gray-bearded teacher in a rust-colored mantle, one hand open toward five seated listeners in modest robes. Woven tents, sunlit rocks, distant hills and leafy branches surround the gathering.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative wilderness teaching gathering expresses the judgments being set before the people. The teacher and attentive listeners make that presentation visible; their faces, garments and camp are artistic choices, not details supplied by this verse or historical likenesses. The teacher is human and does not portray God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A gray-bearded man in a cream robe, head covering and brown mantle sits on sandstone, looking toward sunlight breaking through clouds. One hand is open near his chest and the other rests on his knee. Rocky ridges and sparse desert plants surround him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive posture illustrates the LORD speaking to him. His appearance, clothing, rocky setting and sunlight are imaginative choices; this verse does not specify those details or yet state the message. God remains unseen, and no later commands are illustrated.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Ten cream curtains with colorful woven bands and paired winged figures hang from a wooden beam. Ivory, blue, purple and scarlet yarn and a wooden shuttle lie on a sunlit table against desert hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The ten displayed textiles and colored yarn visualize the tabernacle's prescribed materials and skilled workmanship. The woven winged guardians stand for the cherubim; their form and the desert work setting are imaginative choices, since the verse gives instructions rather than describing this display.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of four robed men kneeling on a rocky ledge, with a larger gathering behind them. Two foreground men bow their heads; two older men look toward a distant, cloud-touched mountain above a winding path. Cream, rust, ochre and blue cloth contrasts with sunlit stone.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The four foreground figures imaginatively represent Moses, Aaron, Nadab and Abihu; the receding gathering represents the seventy elders without a countable reconstruction. Kneeling figures and the open climb toward distant heights illustrate the command to come up and worship from afar. The scene anticipates that instruction; clothing and landscape are artistic conventions, and God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An open-topped square wooden altar body with richly grained amber planks stands on desert sand beneath an acacia tree. Stacked boards, a wooden mallet, a measuring rod and curled shavings lie nearby, with rocky hills in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative construction-stage view emphasizes the commanded acacia wood and square form, with proportions intended to evoke five-cubit sides and a three-cubit height. The exposed timber body, joinery, tools, tree and wilderness workshop are illustrative choices, not a documented reconstruction. It shows preparation rather than a completed altar in use.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A robed keeper holds a tawny bull's rope beside two cream-colored rams with curled horns. Linen courtyard hangings and a brown tent stand behind them beneath a blue sky and dry hills, with stones and small plants in warm sunlight.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The one bull and two rams visualize the animals specified for priestly consecration. The keeper and wilderness sanctuary are imaginative setting choices: the verse gives instructions rather than narrating this gathering. Their calm preparation anticipates the sacred purpose without depicting a completed sacrifice. God is not portrayed.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two elderly bearded men face one another in a sunlit desert camp. The man at left extends an open hand; the man in an ochre mantle holds a hand to his chest. Four younger bearded men stand beside him in blue, rust, green and cream robes. Tents, distant people, mountains and a leafy tree fill the watercolor setting.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering gives visual form to God's instruction: Moses beckons Aaron and his four sons from Israel's camp for priestly service. Their plain robes keep the focus on the call rather than a later investiture. The faces, clothing, tree, tents and desert landscape are artistic conventions; God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an unfinished wooden altar beneath a woven desert shelter. Its open side reveals fitted joints; spare boards, wood shavings, a mallet and a metal blade lie nearby. A bowl of pale resin sits on a workbench, with an acacia tree and blue hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined workshop connects the command to make an incense altar with its specified acacia wood. Exposed joinery and spare boards emphasize construction; the unlit resin suggests its intended use. The shelter, tools and exact altar design are artistic choices, not a construction event narrated in the verse or an archaeological reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a gray-bearded man in a cream robe and red mantle surrounded by anxious people. One man points toward a rocky mountain while others appeal with open hands. Woven tents fill the sunlit desert camp.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The central elder imaginatively represents Aaron. The crowd's urgent gestures and the mountain evoke Israel's impatience at Moses's delay and their demand for gods to lead them. Moses remains absent, and no idol is shown because this verse records the demand before its making. Faces, garments and camp details are imaginative conventions, not historical portraits.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in a cream robe, pale head covering and rust-brown mantle sits on desert rocks, hands on his knees, looking toward a bright opening in the clouds. Ochre cliffs, sparse shrubs and distant lavender ridges surround him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses is imagined listening reverently as the LORD addresses him. The solitary desert setting, his appearance, seated posture and cloud-lit sky are artistic choices, not details supplied in this verse. God remains unseen; the scene does not anticipate the instructions that follow.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly bearded man in a cream robe, rust-colored mantle and cloth head covering shapes the edge of a blank stone tablet with a chisel and wooden mallet. A second blank tablet rests beside it on a rocky ledge amid sunlit mountain slopes and sparse shrubs.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses preparing two blank tablets imaginatively illustrates the commanded replacement of the ones he broke. Their empty faces leave the promised writing to the LORD. The verse records a command and promise rather than this work scene; the tools, clothing and wilderness setting are artistic conventions, not historical certainties. God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, gray-bearded man in a russet cloak holds a wooden staff beside dark tents. Families pack baskets, bedding and water jars while a stony path climbs toward sunlit desert hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined camp-side preparation connects the command to depart and go up with Moses, the people and an ascending wilderness road. The landscape anticipates a journey, not arrival in the promised land. God is unseen; Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are recalled in the promise, not pictured. Clothing and camp details are artistic conventions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a white-bearded elder in cream and rust robes addressing men, women and children in long garments. Seated listeners fill the foreground; rows of tents and rocky desert hills extend beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The people listening to Moses picture the whole congregation being gathered to hear what the LORD commanded them to do. The tents, desert hills, clothing, faces, ages and arrangement are imaginative choices, not details supplied by this verse or historical likenesses. No visible figure represents God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a large, square, open-topped wooden altar body on sandy ground. Cream-sleeved hands stretch a cord along its rim. Wood offcuts, curled shavings and a mallet lie nearby, with a linen shelter and desert hills behind.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The acacia-wood altar body illustrates the material and square proportions specified in Exodus 38:1. The measuring hands, tools and desert shelter are imaginative workshop details. It is shown during wooden construction, before later fittings or metal covering; this is an illustration, not an archaeological reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Under a woven canopy, two bearded artisans carve and measure a wooden piece at a workbench. Behind them, one man weaves colored cloth and another works on a gold-colored ring. Yarn, folded fabrics, tools and fittings fill the foreground, with camp tents and mountains beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The central pair imagines Bezalel and Aholiab among the wise-hearted artisans. Their careful shared work, weaving and metal fittings picture skill used for sanctuary service according to the LORD's command. Faces, ages, clothing and workshop details are imaginative, not specified by this verse; God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded craftsman in a cream robe checks the top edge of a large open wooden chest with a plain rod beneath a woven canopy. Warm wood grain fills the foreground; boards, curled shavings, a mallet and a small metal tool lie nearby, with dry hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Bezalel's careful work on an unadorned acacia-wood ark pictures the maker, material and measured construction named in Exodus 37:1. His appearance, clothing, tools and desert shelter are imaginative staging, not a historical likeness or details supplied by this verse. The image leaves out later fittings; its perspective is illustrative rather than a dimensioned plan.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two linen-sleeved hands prepare an offering: one pours golden oil from a clay jug into fine white flour in a shallow earthenware bowl, while the other steadies its rim. Pale gold resin rests on the flour. Folded linen, a wooden surface and a sunlit tent surround the bowl.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative preparation scene illustrates the fine-flour offering, the oil poured over it and the frankincense placed on it. The unnamed worshipper, vessels and tent setting are artistic choices, not a particular narrated event or an archaeological reconstruction. The LORD is not portrayed.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an elderly bearded man in cream robes and a terracotta mantle standing among sunlit desert rocks, his open hands at his waist and face lifted toward a blue, clouded sky. Low shrubs, dry grasses and lavender hills fill the landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive stance imaginatively conveys his reception of the LORD's speech. The verse does not specify his posture, clothing or surroundings; the wilderness scene supplies a quiet setting without depicting God or inventing the words spoken.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man and a woman sewing a blue garment with purple and scarlet bands inside a sunlit tent. Blue, purple and scarlet yarn, a wooden shuttle and folded cloth rest on their worktable; desert hills and another tent appear beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Two unnamed artisans making blue, purple and scarlet garments visualize the work described in Exodus 39:1. Their identities, tent workshop, garment shapes and arrangement of colors are imaginative choices, not details supplied by the verse. Aaron and Moses are mentioned in the verse but are not shown; God's command is reflected indirectly in the careful work.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in cream robes and a rust-brown mantle kneels beside an open woven tent, one hand over his chest and the other on his knee. Golden desert hills, shrubs, purple flowers and rocks surround him beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' quiet, attentive posture imagines his reception of the LORD's words. The tent, desert, clothing and gesture are artistic setting choices; this verse itself says only that the LORD spoke to Moses, introducing what follows. God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit tent camp, a gray-bearded elder in an ochre robe extends an open hand toward a younger man in cream with a red mantle. The younger man bows his head and holds his hands together. Clay jars, a woven basket, stones and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative camp scene illustrates the verse's conditional law: the elder's appeal suggests the solemn call for testimony, while the younger man's closed mouth and lowered gaze suggest withholding what he knows. His subdued posture evokes bearing guilt. The verse names no particular witness, elder, location or underlying offense; these visual details are illustrative conventions, not a recorded event or historical likeness.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A robed man leads a tawny cow by a rope toward a curtained sanctuary and bronze altar between pale courtyard screens. Warm sunlight falls across the stony ground, with rocky hills beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows one female animal permitted by the verse being presented for a sacrificial peace offering before any slaughter. The healthy cow illustrates the requirement of being without blemish. The anonymous offerer, sanctuary setting, clothing and architecture are illustrative conventions, not details specified by this verse or an archaeological reconstruction. God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, white-bearded man in a cream robe and brown mantle stands with hands folded beside a woven desert tent, gazing upward. Warm light falls across the fabric, sandy stones and distant blue-violet hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive posture imaginatively illustrates the LORD speaking to him. God is not pictured. The desert tent, clothing, landscape and pose are artistic setting choices, not details stated in this verse or a historical likeness. The verse introduces speech without giving its instructions here.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A gray-bearded man in an ivory robe, ochre mantle and head covering stands with clasped hands beside an open woven tent. Sunlight warms the rocky ground, scattered shrubs and distant hills beneath a blue, clouded sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' quiet listening posture imagines his reception of the LORD's address. God remains unseen. The tent, clothing and wilderness are illustrative conventions, not details specified in this verse or claims of historical likeness or archaeological certainty. No later command is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A linen-clad priest holds a ram's lead in a sunlit courtyard. Behind them, flames and smoke rise from a horned bronze altar before a striped tent. A bronze basin and pitcher stand nearby, with hills and a leafy tree beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The priest, living ram, and sanctuary courtyard imaginatively evoke the guilt offering's sacred setting. The verse introduces its law and calls it most holy; it does not narrate this particular moment or specify the animal, clothing, or architecture shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly man in ochre robes extends an open hand toward a gray-bearded man in blue-and-gold linen. Younger men in pale robes stand behind him, while bearded elders surround the gathering among sunlit canvas tents and distant rocky hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' open gesture and the attentive gathering illustrate his call to Aaron, his sons, and Israel's elders. The verse names the eighth day; that timing is not encoded by symbols in the picture. Faces, garments, the tent setting, and the arrangement of people are imaginative conventions, not historical likenesses or an archaeological reconstruction. No later ceremony is shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two elderly bearded men in long robes stand inside a warmly lit woven tent, looking upward toward its open entrance. One wears an ochre mantle and holds a wooden staff; the other wears ivory robes and a linen head covering with his hands folded. Red and blue curtains frame sunlit rocky hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Their quiet shared attention imagines Moses and Aaron receiving the LORD's words. The tent, faces, garments, and staff are illustrative choices; this verse does not specify them, and they are not historical likenesses or archaeological claims. God remains unseen. The particular instructions that follow are not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in ivory robes and linen head coverings hold separate long-handled firepans with glowing coals, small flames and rising smoke before a blue, purple and red tent curtain. Warm watercolor textures cover the sandy courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two priests and their separate smoking firepans imaginatively portray Nadab and Abihu's unauthorized offering. The verse identifies the fire as uncommanded; its appearance alone cannot show that. Their faces, garments and the tent courtyard are artistic conventions, not historical likenesses or archaeological proof. The scene stays with the offering described in verse 1.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in a cream robe and brown mantle sits on a stone at a woven tent entrance, looking upward with his hands resting on his knees. Warm desert light falls across the tent, sandy ground, shrubs and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' quiet, attentive posture imaginatively represents receiving the LORD's words. The verse identifies the speaker and recipient but does not specify the tent, desert setting, clothing, age or posture shown. God is left unseen, and the content of the following message is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two gray-bearded men stand with hands clasped beside a woven tent, looking upward attentively. One wears an ochre mantle; the other wears ivory robes, a rust sash and a linen head covering. Rocky desert hills and sparse shrubs lie behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses and Aaron are imagined listening together beside a wilderness tent, while God remains unseen. Their shared upward attention reflects the LORD addressing both men. The verse does not specify their posture, clothes, surroundings or time of day; these are illustrative choices, not historical likenesses or archaeological claims.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an elderly gray-bearded man in an ivory robe and brown mantle, seated on a stone beside a woven tent. His hands rest on his knees as he looks upward. Sunlit rocky hills, sparse shrubs, and a blue sky surround him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses is imagined listening reverently as the LORD speaks to him. The verse names the speaker and recipient but does not specify a location, appearance, or visible manifestation. The tent, clothing, wilderness, and morning light are artistic context; God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a gray-haired, bearded man in a cream robe and ochre mantle standing inside an open woven tent. He looks upward with a quiet expression and one palm open. Warm sunlight falls across the cloth, sandals and stony ground; low desert hills lie beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses's attentive pose imagines his reception of the LORD's speech. Leviticus 17:1 names the LORD as speaker and Moses as recipient but does not describe a location, appearance or visible manifestation. The tent, clothing and desert are illustrative conventions. God remains unseen, and the painting does not invent the words that follow.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two elderly bearded men in cream robes and blue and russet mantles stand beside an open woven tent, looking upward. Warm sunlight falls on sandy ground, scattered rocks and shrubs, with purple desert hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses and Aaron are imagined listening together as the LORD addresses them. Their clothing, desert tent and afternoon light provide an illustrative setting; this verse does not specify those details. God remains unseen, and no content from the following instructions is depicted. The figures are artistic conventions, not historical likenesses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, gray-bearded man in cream robes and a rust-colored mantle lowers his head, one hand held over his chest, beside a striped fabric tent entrance. Cloth courtyard screens, sandy ground and distant rocky hills surround him in warm watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses listening beside an imagined wilderness sanctuary illustrates the LORD speaking after Aaron's two sons died when they drew near before Him. His bowed posture evokes the sober aftermath; neither their deaths nor God is pictured. The face, garments and tent are artistic conventions, not a historical likeness or archaeological reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in a cream robe and rust-brown mantle stands beside a striped woven tent, looking upward with open hands. Sunlit rocks, sparse shrubs and ochre ridges stretch beneath a pale blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses listening with open hands illustrates his reception of the LORD's speech. His posture, the tent, clothing and wilderness are imaginative context, not details specified in this verse. God remains unseen; the daylight does not give His voice a visible form.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly white-bearded man in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle stands with hands folded beside a desert tent, looking upward. A clay jar and woven baskets rest in the shade; a rocky path winds among shrubs toward distant hills under a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive pose imaginatively conveys his receiving the LORD's speech. His appearance, tent, and desert setting are artistic conventions rather than details stated in this verse. God remains unseen; the illustration focuses on listening before the message is given.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly white-bearded man in a cream robe and brown woven mantle stands beside a tent curtain, gazing upward with one hand over his chest. Sunlit rocks, sparse shrubs and distant hills lie beneath a blue sky in a warm watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive posture imaginatively illustrates his receiving the LORD's words. The tent, clothing, landscape and expression are imagined details that this verse does not specify. God remains unseen; the painting does not attempt to depict the divine speaker or supply the message introduced here.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, gray-bearded man in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle stands beside a woven tent, hands folded at his waist, looking upward across sunlit desert hills under a pale blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses's attentive posture imagines his reception of the LORD's speech. The simple tent, desert landscape, clothing, age and upward gaze are illustrative choices, not details stated in this verse or a historical reconstruction. God remains unseen; no words from the following verses are depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in an ochre mantle speaks with an open hand to two attentive bearded men in ivory robes and linen caps. A fabric sanctuary enclosure, distant tents and rocky hills stand behind them in warm sunlight.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows Moses conveying the LORD's instruction to Aaronic priests. Their attentive stance represents receiving the prohibition against ritual defilement for the dead; no death event is pictured. The faces, clothing and tent setting are illustrative conventions, not established likenesses or archaeological proof.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, white-bearded man in a cream robe, rust-brown mantle and headcloth stands with his hands together beside an open canvas tent. He looks upward in a sunlit, rocky wilderness with distant mauve hills and a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' quiet, attentive posture imagines his reception of the LORD's speech. God remains unseen. The tent, wilderness, clothing and daylight are illustrative choices, since this verse names the speaker and listener without specifying these visual details or the message's content.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an elderly, gray-bearded man in an ivory robe, ochre-brown mantle and sandals, standing with hands together on a rocky desert ledge. He looks upward toward sunlit cliffs beneath a blue sky with pale clouds; lavender ridges recede into the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' listening posture imagines his reception of the LORD's speech on Sinai. The verse names the speaker, hearer and mountain but gives no pose, clothing, weather or mountain profile; these are illustrative choices. God remains unseen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in a cream robe, brown woven mantle and headcloth stands with hands folded beside an open desert tent, gazing upward. Warm watercolor washes show rocky sand, sparse shrubs, distant ridges and a blue, cloud-streaked sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive posture imaginatively expresses the LORD speaking to him. God is not depicted. The tent, wilderness, clothing and gesture provide a contextual setting; Leviticus 24:1 does not specify them or disclose the message that follows. The supplied reference guided watercolor style only, not identity or historical reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a cream tunic and rust mantle seated beside a child in ochre outside a woven tent. He gestures with an open hand. A rough stone, wooden mallet and chisel rest on a low stone bench, with a clay jar, basket, flowers and sunlit hills nearby.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined artisan teaching a child illustrates choosing obedience. The unworked stone and resting tools suggest refusing to fashion objects for worship. The verse records no workshop encounter; it prohibits idols and worship stones, not useful craftsmanship. The figures and setting are illustrative conventions, and God is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two parchment scrolls tied with linen rest on a woven mat beneath a tent awning. A winding desert path passes distant tents toward a sunlit pink-gold mountain under a blue sky and white clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two closed scrolls are an imaginative motif for the family record; the mountain and desert camp evoke Sinai. The verse does not describe these objects, a scene of writing, or a gathering of Aaron's family. The LORD is not depicted, and the landscape is not an archaeological reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An older gray-bearded man in a cream robe, pale head covering, and rust-brown mantle sits on a rock, gazing upward. A woven tent stands behind him amid sandy ground, scrub, and lavender-brown desert hills beneath a blue sky. Fine contours and warm watercolor washes show textured paper.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive upward gaze illustrates his role as the listener while the LORD remains unseen. The desert tent, seated posture, clothing, and morning light are imaginative setting choices, not details specified in this verse or historical likenesses. The scene does not depict the later instructions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two elderly, bearded men in earth-brown and cream robes stand beside an open striped fabric tent, looking upward with attentive expressions. Desert tents and pale rocky hills recede behind them in warm watercolor washes.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two elders' attentive upward gaze imagines Moses and Aaron receiving the LORD's speech. The tent, wilderness camp, faces, and clothing are illustrative choices; this verse does not specify them. God remains unseen, and no later instructions are pictured. The figures are not historical likenesses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly white-bearded man in a cream robe and rust-brown mantle sits at a woven tent entrance, looking upward with one hand against his chest. Golden desert ground, scattered shrubs and distant hills extend beneath a blue sky with pale clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses listening beside a tent imaginatively relates to the LORD speaking to him. His attentive posture expresses reverence; the verse does not specify this pose, tent, landscape or lighting. God remains unseen, and no content from the following instructions is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in layered cream, rust and blue-gray robes stands at a woven tent entrance, looking upward. Sunlit rocky hills, shrubs and two small tents extend behind him; a basket and clay jar rest in the shade.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive upward gaze imaginatively represents his receiving the LORD's speech. The tent, desert landscape, clothing and appearance are illustrative choices, not details specified in this verse or a historical likeness. God remains unseen, with no visible figure or symbolic substitute.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two elderly, gray-bearded men stand beside a cream-and-blue curtained tent in a sunlit desert camp. One wears a brown mantle and holds a wooden staff; the other wears ivory and blue robes with clasped hands. Both look upward, with distant tents and rocky hills behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses and Aaron are imagined listening together as the LORD addresses them. God remains unseen. The wilderness tent, clothing and poses provide an illustrative setting; Numbers 4:1 itself names the two listeners and introduces divine speech, but does not specify these visual details. The artwork is imaginative, not a historical likeness or archaeological reconstruction. Human artwork review is pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in a cream robe and russet mantle stands beside the open entrance of a woven tent, one hand over his chest, amid sunlit desert rocks and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive posture imagines his reception of the LORD's speech. The tent, desert, clothing and appearance supply illustrative context; they are not specified in this verse. God is not depicted, and the following instruction is not anticipated.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an elderly, gray-bearded man in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle standing beside rocks and small flowers, looking upward. Woven tents sit below rose and violet desert mountains in warm sunlight.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive posture imaginatively conveys his receiving the LORD's speech. Tents and rocky mountains evoke the Sinai wilderness; their design, his appearance and the morning light are illustrative choices, not details specified by this verse or verified reconstructions. God is not depicted. The date and the words of the speech are not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, white-bearded Moses holds a small oil flask and touches a horned bronze altar. Bronze bowls and a long-handled utensil rest on a woven mat. Behind him, a brown tabernacle with a blue, purple and red entrance stands within white courtyard hangings amid sandy hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses applying oil to one altar corner is an imaginative representative moment of the verse's wider anointing and consecration. The erected tabernacle and nearby utensils recall the sanctuary, its furnishings and altar implements being set apart. His appearance, clothing, gesture, layout and sanctuary details are illustrative conventions, not a historical likeness or an exact reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of six robed adults among desert tents. Several gesture with troubled expressions while a man turns toward a tent engulfed in orange flames at the camp's edge. Dark smoke rises above the rocky wilderness and distant ridges.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined wilderness camp links the people's troubled exchange with the LORD's fire at the camp's edge. The burning tent represents the verse's consuming judgment without depicting injured people. The clothing, faces, tents, daylight and layout are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse; God is not portrayed.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, gray-bearded man in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle stands with clasped hands beside an open woven tent. Sunlit rocks, desert shrubs, distant tents and purple-brown hills surround him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive pose imaginatively conveys his receiving the LORD's speech. The wilderness tent, clothing and daylight supply an illustrative setting not specified in this verse. God is not depicted, and the later instruction is not added. Moses' appearance is an imaginative convention, not a historical likeness.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly woman in an ochre headscarf and terracotta robe gestures toward a white-bearded man in cream and brown. They face each other solemnly among woven tents, a clay jar, rocky ground and distant sunlit hills, painted in textured watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Miriam and Aaron's sober exchange pictures their criticism of Moses concerning his Cushite wife. The camp, gestures, faces and clothing are imaginative conventions; the verse gives their speech and its occasion without describing their appearance or exact surroundings. Moses and his wife remain outside the frame.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly silver-haired, bearded man in an ivory robe and ochre-brown mantle stands beside a woven tent, hands resting together and eyes lifted. Sandy hills, scattered shrubs, stones, and distant tents sit beneath a pale blue sky in a warm watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' quiet upward attention imaginatively conveys his receiving the LORD's words. The tent, wilderness landscape, clothing, pose, and morning light are artistic choices, not details stated in this verse. God remains unseen; the image does not depict the content of the speech that follows.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor crowd weeps among tents under a starry night sky. In warm lamplight, an elderly man bows with a hand to his forehead, a bearded man cries with his face raised, and a woman wipes her cheek with her shawl. More mourners fill the camp beneath rocky hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The gathered mourners visualize the congregation's raised cry and weeping that night. The anonymous figures, wilderness tents, lamp, clothing and rocky terrain are imaginative contextual choices, not details specified by this verse or claims of historical reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four bearded men in long cream robes and ochre, olive, rust, and blue shawls gather among brown desert tents. The man at left extends an open hand while the others listen thoughtfully. Rocky scrubland and distant hills glow beneath a soft blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The four men represent Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and On. Their imagined gathering visualizes the opening action of Numbers 16:1. The tents, clothing, faces, and gestures are artistic choices, not details specified in this verse or historical likenesses. The named ancestors identify family lines and are not portrayed as people present at the gathering.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in an ivory robe and rust-colored mantle stands beside a woven desert tent with one hand against his chest. Rocky sand, sparse shrubs and distant mauve hills lie beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive pose imaginatively represents his receiving the LORD's speech. The tent, wilderness setting, clothing and gesture are artistic choices rather than details specified in this verse; his appearance is not a historical likeness. God remains unseen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A silver-bearded man in a blue priestly robe and jeweled breastpiece stands between two men in cream robes before a closed purple-and-blue tent curtain. Two men wait behind them in a sunlit desert courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Aaron and his sons are imagined beside the closed sanctuary, with two relatives behind them. Their solemn posture evokes shared accountability for sanctuary offenses and the priests' particular accountability for their priesthood. The verse records the LORD's command; it does not specify these poses or this gathering. Faces, garments and tent details are artistic conventions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two elderly, white-bearded men in cream robes and brown and blue mantles stand with clasped hands beside a striped woven tent, looking upward. Warm sunlight falls over a rocky desert path, dry grasses, distant tents and pale hills beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses and Aaron are imagined listening together to the LORD, who remains unseen. Their posture, faces, clothing and wilderness tent setting are illustrative choices; the verse specifies the speaker and hearers but not these details. The image does not depict the command that follows.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bound captives in earth-toned and blue robes walk along a rocky desert road between spear-carrying guards. A crowned ruler in a red cloak watches from the left; tents stand in the distance beneath pale hills and a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative aftermath represents the verse's capture of Israelites by Arad's forces. The king, guarded prisoners and dry road make that conflict visible without depicting the fighting. Faces, clothing, restraints, tents and landscape details are illustrative choices; the verse gives neither the prisoners' number nor these particulars.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four robed mourners stand beside a low stone-covered grave in a sunlit rocky wilderness. One woman holds her head covering to her face while a man rests a hand on her shoulder. Tents and small groups of people spread across the valley behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The closed grave represents Miriam's burial at Kadesh, and the tents evoke Israel's congregation staying in the wilderness of Zin. The anonymous mourners, their gestures, the grave's form, the landscape and the warm light are imaginative details, not descriptions supplied by the verse or an archaeological reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a woman and child beside two men settling among brown tents. One man kneels with a mallet beside a tent peg; the other bends over rolled bedding. Clay jars, bundles and a basket rest nearby. A blue river separates the camp from a small distant settlement beneath hazy hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The camp beside the river illustrates Israel stopping on the plains of Moab opposite Jericho. The family, tent work, warm light and distant settlement are imaginative details that make the arrival visible; the verse does not name these people or describe these activities. Clothing, vegetation and buildings are illustrative conventions, not historical or archaeological claims.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream robe, rust-colored mantle, and cloth head covering stands on a rocky ridge, looking across a sunlit, sparsely vegetated wilderness toward distant blue-purple hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Balaam's still posture and gaze toward the wilderness illustrate the turn described in the verse. His empty, resting hands avoid depicting the divination he no longer seeks on this occasion. His likeness, clothing, terrain, and daylight are imaginative conventions; the Lord's intention to bless Israel is explained by the verse rather than made physically visible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men approach two women in long dresses and shawls beside a shaded woven tent. The nearer man holds his hand to his chin. A path leads back to many tents across a sunlit plain, with trees, flowers and distant hills in warm watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The men approaching the women at a tent apart from the camp indirectly evoke the beginning of the sexual immorality named in the verse; no sexual act is shown. Their poses, clothes, tent, vegetation and landscape are imaginative choices, not details supplied by the verse or a verified reconstruction of Shittim.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of two bearded men in long cream robes beside a woven desert tent. The older man wears a rust-colored mantle; the other has a white head covering and striped sash. Both look upward. A clay jar, shrubs, distant tents and pale mountains fill the sunlit setting.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two attentive men imaginatively represent Moses and Eleazar receiving the LORD's words. God remains unseen. Their faces, clothing, upward gaze and wilderness tent setting are artistic choices, not details supplied by this verse or established historical likenesses. Aaron is identified as Eleazar's father and is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly white-bearded man in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle stands beside an open woven tent, gazing upward with a peaceful expression. Other tents lie among sunlit rocky hills, shrubs, grasses, and small white flowers beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses is imagined listening reverently as the LORD speaks. God remains unseen. The wilderness camp, clothing, expression, and morning light are illustrative choices; this verse does not specify them or give the message that follows. The scene conveys attentive reception without inventing the words spoken.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five women in long terracotta, blue, olive, ochre and cream garments walk together along a sunlit sandy path. One rests her hand on the central woman's arm. Woven tents, sparse scrub and dry hills surround them beneath a blue sky in a textured watercolor painting.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The five sisters approaching together illustrate the verse's opening action and its naming of Zelophehad's daughters. Their faces, ages, clothing and the wilderness camp are imaginative conventions, not historical likenesses or a setting specified in this verse. The named ancestors are not pictured, and the later hearing and inheritance decision are not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man in an ivory robe sounds a long silver trumpet as smiling adults and children gather among woven tents. A work tool and basket rest beside a tent, with sunlit hills beyond, all painted in warm, textured watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The trumpet and gathered community imagine the holy assembly and day of trumpet blasts commanded in the verse. The unused tool and basket suggest ordinary labor set aside. The people, tents, landscape and trumpet design are illustrative choices, not details supplied by the verse; the first day of the seventh month is conveyed by the Scripture rather than a visual date.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly white-bearded man in a cream robe and brown mantle stands beside a woven desert tent, one hand on his chest as he looks upward. Small tents, rocky hills, shrubs and pale clouds fill the sunlit watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive posture imaginatively relates to the LORD speaking to him. The tent, landscape, clothing and upward gaze are artistic context, not details stated in Numbers 31:1. God remains unseen, and the message introduced by this verse is not depicted. This is an imaginative portrayal, not a historical likeness. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed herders stand on a rocky rise beneath a leafy tree, looking across sunlit green hills filled with grazing cattle, sheep and goats. One gestures toward the pasture; blue hills recede beneath a clear sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The three unnamed herders imaginatively represent members of the tribes of Reuben and Gad observing land suitable for their abundant livestock. They are not the patriarchs themselves. The grassy hills suggest Jazer and Gilead without claiming an exact historical view; the scene does not depict a later agreement or grant of land.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly, white-bearded Moses in cream robes and a russet mantle gestures as Israelite men, women and children listen among dark tents, rocky ground and distant hills in warm sunlight.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative camp gathering illustrates Moses communicating the LORD's instructions to Israel. Attentive listeners express reverence and readiness to hear. Their appearance, clothing and camp arrangement are artistic choices; the verse does not specify them. God is not depicted. The supplied Hebrew verse corresponds to Numbers 29:40 in the KJV.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly white-bearded man in a cream robe, rust-colored mantle and head covering sits on a rock beside a woven tent. He looks upward with both hands resting on his knees, amid sunlit stones, dry grasses and ochre hills beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive posture illustrates his receiving the LORD's speech. The verse does not specify his posture or surroundings; the tent, clothing and wilderness are imaginative choices, not historical certainties. God remains unseen, and the image does not anticipate the message of later verses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two elderly bearded men in cream robes and blue and rust-colored mantles lead a long procession along a rocky path. One carries a wooden staff. Behind them, a mother holds a child's hand; families, laden donkeys and sheep follow from green fields and distant dwellings toward sunlit, sandy hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two elders imaginatively represent Moses and Aaron, and the grouped family procession evokes Israel leaving Egypt in organized hosts. The winding road illustrates the journeys introduced by the verse. Clothing, animals, fields, dwellings and terrain are illustrative choices, not details specified here or a reconstruction of a particular route or stop.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a white-bearded elder in a cream robe and brown mantle, holding a wooden staff beside a blue river. Tents stand behind him; reeds, golden grasses, rocks and flowers line the near bank, with a small settlement and sunlit hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Moses' attentive stance beside the Jordan illustrates his receiving the LORD's speech on Moab's plains opposite Jericho. His appearance, clothing, tents, vegetation and the distant settlement are imaginative details, not historical reconstructions. God remains unseen; this introductory verse does not depict the commands that follow.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of robed travelers carrying bundles and staffs along a winding rocky path beneath vast sunlit rust-colored mountains. A woman rests her arm around a child in the foreground while the procession recedes among sparse shrubs.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The long curving procession and rugged hills imagine Israel's prolonged journey around Seir. The families, clothes, path and terrain are illustrative choices, not details supplied by this verse or a verified route. No sea crossing is shown: the verse names the Red Sea route. God's command is conveyed through the journey without depicting Him.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Men in earth-toned tunics carry round shields and spears along a winding rocky road. Across the open path, a bearded leader in a red-brown cloak approaches with ranks of soldiers from a hilltop walled town. Golden hills, scattered trees, flowers and blue mountains frame the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The ascending road and approaching forces imagine Israel's movement toward Bashan and Og's coming out to battle at Edrei. The red-cloaked leader represents Og; the open road holds the encounter before fighting, without showing its outcome. Faces, dress, terrain and town are imaginative conventions, not historical likenesses or archaeological reconstructions. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed, bearded men stand before a seated white-bearded elder and three listening men beneath a woven awning. The foremost visitor extends an open hand. Dark tents, scrub and sunlit hills fill the background of the warm watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The approaching elders and attentive listeners imaginatively depict the clan heads speaking before Moses and Israel's leaders. The verse names their ancestry, so Gilead, Machir, Manasseh and Joseph are not shown as participants. The number of men, faces, garments, awning and camp landscape are artistic staging, not details specified by the verse or verified historical likenesses. The scene does not anticipate the petition's later content.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly white-bearded teacher in a cream robe and rust-colored mantle gestures to attentive adults and children beneath a leafy tree. A blue river winds through sunlit green and golden hills behind them in a textured watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined teaching circle connects learning the LORD's commands with putting them into practice in the land ahead. The river and sunlit countryside suggest the approaching possession; the precise people, clothing, and terrain are illustrative choices, not details supplied by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly white-bearded man in an ivory robe and ochre mantle stands with one palm extended toward families seated in a broad circle. Adults and children look toward him. Fabric tents, low hills and a blue sky lie behind the assembly, painted in warm, finely outlined watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The listening families visualize Moses' call for all Israel to hear. Their attentive posture suggests the readiness to learn and obey that he commands; it does not claim that obedience has already occurred. The camp, faces and clothing are imaginative conventions, not historical likenesses or a precise reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A white-bearded teacher in cream and rust robes gestures while men, women and two children listen beside tents. A winding river and sunlit hills stretch behind them in a detailed, warm watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The elder represents Moses teaching Israel. The listening families illustrate the call to hear and practice the statutes and judgments; the distant valley suggests the land God is giving them, still ahead. Faces, clothing, camp and landscape are imaginative, not historical likenesses or a precise location. God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five robed travelers pause on a rocky path beneath a leafy tree, looking across cultivated fields and a broad valley toward walled hill towns. One holds a staff. Warm golden light washes the stone walls, distant blue hills and textured watercolor sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative, anticipatory view places a small Israelite company before an inhabited, fortified land to evoke nations greater and mightier than Israel. It relates to the LORD's promised bringing-in and casting-out without depicting a particular battle or completed expulsion. The travelers, buildings and terrain are artistic conventions, not identified biblical individuals, a map of the seven nations or an archaeological reconstruction. God is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of six robed travelers, including children and a man holding a staff, beside a blue-green river. Across the water, a large sunlit city rises behind high stone and earthen walls; a second walled settlement stands on a distant hill. Flowers, reeds and an overhanging tree frame the view.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative riverbank view anticipates the crossing and dispossession announced in the verse. The small gathering represents Israel facing stronger nations, suggested by two imposing fortified cities. Their height conveys the verse's formidable defenses without making them literally reach heaven. The people, architecture and combined viewpoint are illustrative conventions, not identified portraits or an archaeological reconstruction. No battle or completed conquest is shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a white-bearded elder in cream and rust robes teaching with an open hand. A man, woman, two children and another elder sit listening among rocks and wildflowers, with canvas tents, sunlit fields and distant hills behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The attentive teaching circle imagines Israel receiving the commandment. Parents and children suggest life and multiplication, while the sunlit fields evoke the promised inheritance. The gathering, faces and landscape are imaginative conventions; the picture does not document a particular assembly or show Moses entering the land.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man, a head-covered woman and a child seated on a woven mat beside a tent. The man holds a hand over his heart and rests the other on a tied scroll. A clay jar, flowers and a folded cloth surround them; a path leads toward hills and distant houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative household composition connects the hand over the heart with love for the LORD and the carefully held closed law scroll with keeping His charge, statutes, judgments and commandments. The continuing path suggests daily faithfulness. The verse commands enduring love and obedience; it does not narrate this family scene. No visible figure represents God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man with a rolled parchment scroll on his lap sits beneath a leafy tree with a listening man, woman and child. Warm watercolor fields, a winding path, scattered trees, distant houses and layered hills extend behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household, closed scroll and sunlit land connect the command to obey with life in the land the LORD gives. The different ages suggest lifelong obedience; they do not depict named fathers or a gathering recorded in the verse. The scroll is a visual convention for the statutes and judgments, and the scenery is not an identified historical site.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly bearded man in cream and rust robes holds a hammer and chisel over a blank stone tablet. A second blank tablet stands beside him, near an open wooden chest and its lid. A rocky path climbs the sunlit mountain behind him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows Moses preparing the two stone tablets and wooden ark commanded in the verse; the rising mountain path recalls the summons to come up. It illustrates the commanded preparations rather than the moment of speech. The face, clothing, chest design and landscape are artistic conventions, not historical evidence. God remains unseen.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two hands in cream and russet sleeves cradle a rolled parchment tied with linen above a woven cloth and wooden table. Brown tent curtains open onto sunlit golden hills beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The intact scroll, carefully supported by ordinary human hands, imaginatively evokes keeping the whole command without alteration. The verse calls for obedience, not merely preserving an object; it does not describe a scroll, tent, or this scene. The setting is illustrative rather than a claim of a historical event or archaeological certainty.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in earth-colored robes face each other at a wooden courtyard table. The man in terracotta handles a loosened cord around a blank rolled scroll; the man in olive holds out empty palms. Seven smooth stones lie along the table beneath olive branches, with a village and hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined encounter pictures the commanded release of debts through a loosened cord around a scroll and a neighbor’s open hands. Seven plain stones suggest the seven-year cycle. The verse does not describe these men, this courtyard, or a stone-counting ritual; these are illustrative choices, not a recorded event or an established historical custom.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a grieving young man seated beside a low stone-ringed earth mound. An older man rests a hand on his arm while a woman in a cream head covering stands behind. Desert tents and dry hills lie beyond; leafy branches frame the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Israelite mourning scene illustrates the command rather than an event narrated in the verse. The grave and family are artistic choices. Their intact skin and unshaved hair show mourning without the forbidden practices. Human comfort suggests the dignity of those addressed as God's children; God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in ivory robes and head coverings share a dish of cooked meat at a wooden table with flatbread and clay bowls. A bronze-colored altar burns behind them beside a fabric enclosure and tent, with fields and low hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined priestly meal illustrates provision from the LORD's offerings rather than a tribal land inheritance. The food is an edible allotted portion, not a wholly burnt offering. Fields beyond the sanctuary suggest Israel's land without showing it granted to Levi. The meal, faces, clothing and tent setting are illustrative choices, not a recorded event or an exact historical reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a warm watercolor landscape, a kneeling man examines the ragged ear of a cream-colored sheep. A standing man raises an open palm and points toward the ear. A brown bull stands beneath an olive tree, with a tent, a bare stone altar and sunlit hills behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined inspection illustrates a command, not a narrated event. The sheep's healed ear defect and the stopping gesture suggest withholding a blemished animal from sacrifice; the bull recalls the other animal named. The verse calls such an offering an abomination to the LORD. The people, specific defect and sanctuary setting are illustrative choices, not identified persons or archaeological claims.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A mother, father and child sit at an open tent. Lamplight illuminates flatbread, a dish of meat and clay vessels on a woven mat. A staff and tied bundle rest beside them. Green grain, flowers, a winding path and distant tents extend beneath a starry blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined family and meal evoke keeping Passover, spring barley suggests Abib, and the night setting, staff and packed bundle recall deliverance from Egypt. These details form a devotional remembrance, not a depiction of a named household or an exact historical reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man lies face turned away in golden grass, wearing a cream tunic and brown mantle. A concerned woman and bearded man stand nearby beneath an olive tree, with stone houses and purple hills beyond. Warm watercolor washes and fine contours depict flowers, rocks, cloth, and textured paper.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined discovery illustrates the verse's conditional case rather than a named historical incident. The two villagers are anonymous illustrative discoverers, not identified witnesses or suspects. The fallen man is shown indirectly, without visible injury; the killer remains unknown. Clothing and landscape are artistic conventions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of cloaked men with round shields and upright spears on a rocky rise. An older man rests a hand on a younger companion's shoulder as they face a sunlit valley filled with a large army, horses and wooden chariots beneath distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined prebattle moment sets a small group of Israelite soldiers before a much larger force with horses and chariots. Their steady posture and reassuring touch suggest the courage commanded in the verse. The LORD remains unseen; His deliverance from Egypt is recalled by the verse. The people, terrain and equipment are artistic conventions rather than a reconstruction of a named battle.
